EdgeGuard - Neo4j Client with Source Tracking
Handles connection, graph operations, and source tracking with data quality

Production-ready features:
- Connection retry logic with exponential backoff
- Comprehensive error handling and logging
- Batch processing for bulk inserts
- Health checks
- Timeouts for all operations
"""

def _log_merge_counter_inspection_kill_switch_once() -> None:
    """PR-N11 follow-up (cursor-bugbot 2026-04-21, Medium): emit ONE
    WARN log at module import when ``EDGEGUARD_DISABLE_MERGE_COUNTER_INSPECTION``
    is set to a truthy value. Promised by the docstring on
    ``_record_batch_counters`` — without this, an on-call operator who
    flips the kill-switch has no log confirmation that the flag took
    effect. In a production incident that's exactly when you need the
    signal most.

    Called unconditionally at module import; short-circuits (no log)
    when the switch is disabled (the default). When enabled, emits
    at WARNING so the line survives the default operator log filter
    but doesn't escalate to ERROR for what is a deliberate ops choice.
    """
    import os as _os

    _val = _os.environ.get("EDGEGUARD_DISABLE_MERGE_COUNTER_INSPECTION", "").strip().lower()
    if _val in ("1", "true", "yes", "on"):
        logger.warning(
            "[KILL-SWITCH-ACTIVE] EDGEGUARD_DISABLE_MERGE_COUNTER_INSPECTION=%r — "
            "_record_batch_counters will short-circuit to no-op. "
            "Ineffective-batch detection (PR-N9 B6) is DISABLED for this process. "
            "This is an ops escape hatch; unset the env var and restart to re-enable.",

        )

def _record_batch_counters(
    *, label: str, source_id: str, batch_len: int, result: Any = None, summary: Any = None
) -> None:
    """PR-N9 B6 (audit 09 Prod Readiness #2, 2026-04-21): inspect Neo4j
    result counters to detect silent-write failures.

    PR-N11 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline ops readiness): honor the
    ``EDGEGUARD_DISABLE_MERGE_COUNTER_INSPECTION`` env var. Pre-PR-N11
    there was no way to disable this helper without a code revert — if
    the inspection itself turned out to have a bug mid-baseline
    (double-consume, API drift, etc.) on-call would be helpless. Set
    env to any truthy value (``1``, ``true``, ``yes``) to short-circuit
    the helper into a no-op. A module-load WARN log (see
    ``_log_merge_counter_inspection_kill_switch_once`` below) emits
    ONE line at startup when the kill-switch is active, so on-call
    can confirm the flag took effect without reading every per-batch
    DEBUG line.

    **The bug this closes:** ``merge_indicators_batch`` and
    ``merge_vulnerabilities_batch`` historically used ``len(batch)``
    as the success_count regardless of what Neo4j actually wrote. If
    the MATCH-into-SOURCED_FROM silently failed (e.g. Source node
    missing, constraint violation, schema mismatch), the outer
    success_count lied and operators had no signal — the batch
    silently produced zero edges.

    **What this helper does:** reads
    ``summary.counters.nodes_created +
    nodes_updated + relationships_created + properties_set``. If ALL
    four are zero on a non-empty batch, emits:

      - ERROR log with label, source, batch size, and counter values
        (so operators see exactly which batch went silent)
      - Increments ``edgeguard_neo4j_merge_ineffective_batch_total``
        Prometheus counter (so Grafana can alert on a non-zero rate)

    A non-empty batch producing zero writes is almost always a bug
    (missing prerequisite nodes, broken schema, constraint violation).
    The rare legitimate case — every item already MERGEd with
    identical properties — still increments ``properties_set`` at
    least via the ``r.updated_at = datetime()`` clauses every batch
    sets, so the all-zero check is a strong signal.

    **Never raises:** defensive wrapped in try/except so a counter
    bug can't break production writes. The metric increment itself
    is None-guarded (PR-N5 R1 pattern).

    2026-10-16: takes the ``summary`` the batch writer read. The server reports an error it meets
    while executing or committing the batch (deadlock, lock or transaction timeout, constraint
    violation) with the result; read here, inside this helper's ``except Exception``, that error was
    logged at DEBUG and the batch counted as written, without retry. ``_execute_batch_with_retry``
    now reads the result inside its retry ``try`` and passes the summary, so the kill switch above
    skips only this inspection, never the read. ``result`` (read here when no summary is given)
    serves callers that pass an unread result.
    """
    # PR-N11 kill-switch: if the helper itself turns out to have a bug
    # mid-baseline (driver API drift, double-consume, etc.) the
    # operator sets EDGEGUARD_DISABLE_MERGE_COUNTER_INSPECTION=1 and
    # restarts the task. Checked every call (cheap env read) so the
    # toggle takes effect on the next batch without a code change.
    import os as _os  # local import to avoid polluting module-level os reuse

    if _os.environ.get("EDGEGUARD_DISABLE_MERGE_COUNTER_INSPECTION", "").strip().lower() in (
        "1",
        "true",
        "yes",
        "on",
    ):
        return
    try:
        if summary is None:
            summary = result.consume()
        counters = summary.counters
        # ``counters`` exposes attributes as ints; absent attrs default
        # to 0 via getattr.
        nodes_created = getattr(counters, "nodes_created", 0)
        nodes_updated = getattr(counters, "nodes_updated", 0) if hasattr(counters, "nodes_updated") else 0
        # Neo4j 5.x uses ``properties_set``; 4.x/5.0 naming is consistent.
        properties_set = getattr(counters, "properties_set", 0)
        rels_created = getattr(counters, "relationships_created", 0)
        rels_updated = (
            getattr(counters, "relationships_updated", 0) if hasattr(counters, "relationships_updated") else 0
        )

        total_touched = nodes_created + nodes_updated + properties_set + rels_created + rels_updated

        if batch_len > 0 and total_touched == 0:
            logger.error(
                "[MERGE-INEFFECTIVE] label=%s source=%s batch_len=%d — Neo4j counters "
                "all zero (nodes_created=%d, nodes_updated=%d, properties_set=%d, "
                "rels_created=%d, rels_updated=%d). The batch silently produced zero "
                "writes. Likely cause: missing prerequisite node (e.g. Source), "
                "constraint violation, or schema mismatch. Operator action: check the "
                "current Source nodes via ``MATCH (s:Source {source_id: '%s'}) RETURN s`` "
                "and re-run ``ensure_sources()`` if missing.",
                label,
                source_id,
                batch_len,
                nodes_created,
                nodes_updated,
                properties_set,
                rels_created,
                rels_updated,
                source_id,
            )
            if _NEO4J_MERGE_INEFFECTIVE_BATCH is not None:
                try:
                    _NEO4J_MERGE_INEFFECTIVE_BATCH.labels(label=label, source=source_id).inc()
                except Exception as _metric_err:
                    # Same non-silent pattern as other metric guards.
                    logger.debug(
                        "ineffective-batch metric increment failed: %s",
                        _metric_err,
                        exc_info=True,
                    )
    except Exception as _inspect_err:
        # Counter inspection itself failed (e.g. driver API change,
        # result already consumed). Log at DEBUG and continue — don't
        # let observability code break a production write.
        logger.debug(
            "result-counter inspection failed for label=%s source=%s: %s",
            label,
            source_id,
            _inspect_err,
            exc_info=True,
        )


def _execute_batch_with_retry(
    driver,
    query: str,
    *,
    label: str,
    source_id: str,
    batch_len: int,
    query_kwargs: dict,
    max_retries: int = 3,
    base_delay: float = 2.0,
):
    """PR-N15 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit Fix #2 + #3): run a batch
    MERGE with retry-on-transient semantics, inspect result counters,
    and emit a Prometheus counter on permanent failure.

    Pre-PR-N15, ``merge_indicators_batch`` and ``merge_vulnerabilities_batch``
    both had a bare ``except Exception: error_count += len(batch)`` that
    logged an ERROR and silently counted the entire batch as failed.
    A 5-second Neo4j GC pause or a brief deadlock dropped 1000 nodes
    per batch with no retry, no dedicated counter, and no operator
    signal beyond one WARN log line. Over a 730d baseline with ~30
    sync cycles, thousands of nodes were silently lost.

    This helper:

    1. Retries on transient Neo4j errors (``ServiceUnavailable`` /
       ``TransientError`` / ``DatabaseError`` with a retryable ``.code`` —
       via the same classifier used by the ``retry_with_backoff``
       decorator) with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s).
    2. Reads the result inside the retry ``try`` (2026-10-16: an execution
       or commit error arrives with it), then runs ``_record_batch_counters``
       on its summary to catch silent-write failures (PR-N9 B6).
    3. On PERMANENT failure (retries exhausted, or non-retryable
       exception), emits ``edgeguard_neo4j_batch_permanent_failure_total``
       so operators can alert on silent data loss.

    Returns: ``(ok: bool, rows_attempted: int)``. On success ``ok=True``
    and ``rows_attempted = batch_len``. On permanent failure ``ok=False``
    and the caller counts ``batch_len`` as errors.
    """
    last_exc: Optional[BaseException] = None
    for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
        try:
            with driver.session() as session:
                result = session.run(query, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT, **query_kwargs)
                # 2026-10-16: the server reports an error it meets while executing or committing
                # the batch (deadlock, lock or transaction timeout, constraint violation) with the
                # result, not when run() returns: read it here, inside this try, so the retry
                # classifier below sees it (an unread result is read by Session.close, which only
                # logs the error).
                summary = result.consume()
            # B6 counter inspection (PR-N9) on the summary already read; never raises.
            _record_batch_counters(
                label=label,
                source_id=source_id,
                batch_len=batch_len,
                summary=summary,
            )
            return True, batch_len
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — retry classifier below
            last_exc = e
            if not _is_retryable_neo4j_error(e):
                # Non-retryable — log + emit permanent-failure counter + stop retrying.
                logger.error(
                    "[BATCH-PERMANENT-FAILURE] label=%s source=%s batch_len=%d — non-retryable error %s: %s",
                    label,
                    source_id,
                    batch_len,
                    type(e).__name__,
                    e,
                )
                _emit_batch_permanent_failure(label=label, source_id=source_id, reason="non_retryable")
                return False, batch_len
            if attempt >= max_retries:
                break
            delay = base_delay * (2**attempt)
            code = getattr(e, "code", "")
            logger.warning(
                "[BATCH-RETRY] label=%s source=%s batch_len=%d attempt=%d/%d: %s%s — retrying in %.1fs",
                label,
                source_id,
                batch_len,
                attempt + 1,
                max_retries + 1,
                type(e).__name__,
                f" [{code}]" if code else "",
                delay,
            )
            time.sleep(delay)
    # Retries exhausted.
    logger.error(
        "[BATCH-PERMANENT-FAILURE] label=%s source=%s batch_len=%d — "
        "transient error persisted after %d retries: %s: %s",
        label,
        source_id,
        batch_len,
        max_retries,
        type(last_exc).__name__ if last_exc else "UNKNOWN",
        last_exc,
    )
    _emit_batch_permanent_failure(label=label, source_id=source_id, reason="retries_exhausted")
    return False, batch_len


def _emit_batch_permanent_failure(*, label: str, source_id: str, reason: str) -> None:
    """PR-N15: emit the permanent-failure counter. None-guarded
    (mirrors PR-N5 R1 pattern). Reason is a bounded enum
    (``non_retryable`` / ``retries_exhausted``)."""
    if _NEO4J_BATCH_PERMANENT_FAILURES is None:
        return
    try:
        _NEO4J_BATCH_PERMANENT_FAILURES.labels(
            label=label,
            source=source_id,
            reason=reason,
        ).inc()
    except Exception as _metric_err:
        logger.debug(
            "batch-permanent-failure metric increment failed: %s",
            _metric_err,
            exc_info=True,
        )


# Configuration constants
NEO4J_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT = 60  # seconds
# seconds; 120 s was too low for a 441K-node graph and 300 s for the 730-day "Indicator -> Malware
# (family match)" link query (289 s on 2026-10-13, 316 s with MalwareBazaar and ATT&CK for ICS added).
# 2026-10: 3600 s (was 900). The timeouts are protection against a statement that hangs, not a
# budget: loose enough that a slow statement on the graph of a 730-day baseline never reaches them,
# well inside the Airflow task limits (5–6 h). A statement aborted at its timeout is logged as
# ``[NEO4J-TIMEOUT]`` (``_TimeoutSession``).
NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT = int(os.getenv("EDGEGUARD_NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT", "3600"))
# Relationship UNWIND batches (2026-10: 600 s, was 60): a batch takes seconds; the limit only stops one that
# hangs. Deadlocks are reported by Neo4j at once and retried by the batch writer.
_REL_QUERY_TIMEOUT = 600  # seconds

# Every column ``apoc.periodic.iterate`` yields that a caller needs to judge a batched step.
# ``errorMessages`` alone is not enough: a Neo4j heap OOM inside a batch came back with an
# empty ``errorMessages`` and only ``failedBatches`` / ``batch.errors`` set (local 800-day
# baseline, 2026-09-16).
APOC_ITERATE_YIELD = (
    "batches, total, errorMessages, failedBatches, failedOperations, wasTerminated, batch, operations, updateStatistics"
)


def apoc_iterate_failures(row) -> list:
    """Return the failure signals in an ``apoc.periodic.iterate`` result row.

    ``row`` is a ``neo4j.Record`` or a dict with the ``APOC_ITERATE_YIELD`` columns.
    Columns missing from the row (older callers, mocks) count as clean. ``errorMessages``
    is a map ``{message: count}``, so the result is a list of strings, never the map.
    """
    failures = []
    if row.get("errorMessages"):
        failures.append(f"errorMessages={row['errorMessages']}")
    if row.get("failedBatches"):
        failures.append(f"failedBatches={row['failedBatches']}")
    if row.get("failedOperations"):
        failures.append(f"failedOperations={row['failedOperations']}")
    if row.get("wasTerminated"):
        failures.append("wasTerminated=true")
    for column in ("batch", "operations"):
        errors = (row.get(column) or {}).get("errors")
        if errors:
            failures.append(f"{column}.errors={errors}")
    return failures


class RelationshipBatchResult(int):
    """Return value of ``Neo4jClient.create_misp_relationships_batch``.

    An ``int`` equal to the number of relationship rows written, so callers that add or
    compare the return value keep working unchanged. ``failed`` additionally carries the
    number of rows dropped by batches that failed permanently (non-retryable Neo4j error
    or retries exhausted), so callers can account for the loss instead of treating the
    attempted row count as the written count.

    2026-10 (curated packages): the curated templates MATCH both ends, so a claim whose
    subject or object is not in the graph writes nothing. ``curated_sent`` counts the curated
    rows of the batches that ran, ``curated_matched`` those that found both ends (the
    templates' ``count(r)``), and only the matched ones count in the ``int`` value.
    ``curated_missing`` is a bounded sample of the ends that were not found, as
    ``"<Label> '<name or id>'"``.
    """

    failed: int
    curated_sent: int
    curated_matched: int
    curated_missing: Tuple[str, ...]

    def __new__(
        cls,
        written: int,
        failed: int = 0,
        curated_sent: int = 0,
        curated_matched: int = 0,
        curated_missing: Sequence[str] = (),
    ) -> "RelationshipBatchResult":
        obj = super().__new__(cls, int(written))
        obj.failed = int(failed)
        obj.curated_sent = int(curated_sent)
        obj.curated_matched = int(curated_matched)
        obj.curated_missing = tuple(curated_missing)
        return obj


# 2026-10 (curated packages): how many names of missing ends one batch reports.
CURATED_MISSING_SAMPLE = 20


def _curated_matched_count(result: Any, sent: int) -> int:
    """The ``count(r) AS matched`` a curated template returns, at most ``sent`` (2026-10).

    A driver result always carries it; a result without one (a test double) keeps the earlier
    reading, every row sent counts as written.
    """
    record = result.single() if hasattr(result, "single") else None
    try:
        value = record["matched"] if record is not None else None
    except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
        value = None
    if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0:
        return min(value, sent)
    return sent


# ``(label, key, row field)`` of the subject and the object a curated template MATCHes.
_CuratedEnds = Tuple[Tuple[str, str, str], Tuple[str, str, str]]


def _curated_missing_query(subject: Tuple[str, str, str], obj: Tuple[str, str, str]) -> str:
    """Read-only Cypher naming the ends a curated template's rows did not find (2026-10).

    ``subject`` / ``obj`` are ``(label, key, row field)`` of the template's two MATCHes. Each
    returned row has the missing subject and / or object (the other column is null), bounded
    by ``$limit``.
    """
    (s_label, s_key, s_field), (o_label, o_key, o_field) = subject, obj
    _validate_label(s_label)
    _validate_label(o_label)
    return (
        "UNWIND $rows AS row "
        f"OPTIONAL MATCH (s:{s_label} {{{s_key}: row.{s_field}}}) "
        f"OPTIONAL MATCH (o:{o_label} {{{o_key}: row.{o_field}}}) "
        "WITH row, s, o WHERE s IS NULL OR o IS NULL "
        f"RETURN CASE WHEN s IS NULL THEN row.{s_field} END AS subject, "
        f"CASE WHEN o IS NULL THEN row.{o_field} END AS object "
        "LIMIT $limit"
    )

def _validate_label(label: str) -> str:
    """Raise ValueError if *label* is not in the allowed set, else return it."""
    if label not in _ALLOWED_NODE_LABELS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cypher injection guard: '{label}' is not an allowed node label. Allowed: {sorted(_ALLOWED_NODE_LABELS)}"
        )
    return label


def _clear_scope_pattern(label: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """Node pattern of the edgeguard-only clear (2026-10): ``(n)``, or ``(n:<label>)`` when one
    allow-listed label narrows it (``scripts/clear_neo4j.py --label``); raises ValueError otherwise."""
    return "(n)" if label is None else f"(n:{_validate_label(label)})"


class _ClearProgress:
    """What one attempt of ``clear_all`` / ``clear_edgeguard_managed`` has deleted so far, counted
    batch by batch, so the audit line of an attempt that fails part-way names it (2026-10-23)."""

    __slots__ = ("nodes", "relationships")

    def __init__(self) -> None:

# Compiled regex for validating Cypher property/relationship names.
# Allows only identifiers: letter or underscore, followed by letters/digits/underscores.
_PROP_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$")


def _validate_rel_type(name: str) -> str:
    """Raise ValueError if *name* is not a safe Cypher relationship-type identifier."""
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(name):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cypher injection guard: '{name}' is not a valid relationship type name. "
            "Only alphanumeric characters and underscores are allowed."
        )
    return name


def _mark_deprecated(data: Dict[str, Any], extra_props: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """``n.deprecated = true`` for an item ATT&CK deprecated (2026-10).

    ATT&CK retires an object without a successor with ``x_mitre_deprecated: true``. The node and
    its links stay; the flag lets consumers filter (``WHERE coalesce(n.deprecated, false) = false``).
    Set only, never cleared: another source's item about the same node says nothing about it.
    """
    if data.get("deprecated") is True:
        extra_props["deprecated"] = True


def _validate_prop_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Raise ValueError if *name* is not a safe Cypher property identifier."""
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(name):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cypher injection guard: '{name}' is not a valid property name. "
            "Only alphanumeric characters and underscores are allowed."
        )
    return name


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Zone accumulation — override 'global' if any specific sector exists
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# PR #34 round 24: the per-text/per-item zone detection in ``config.py`` and
# the MISP writer enforce the rule "if a specific sector matches, drop
# 'global' from the zone list." But the Neo4j MERGE layer used to accumulate
# zones with a plain APOC set union — so an Indicator first ingested from a
# healthcare-specific feed (zone=["healthcare"]) and later seen by a generic
# feed (zone=["global"]) would accumulate to ``n.zone = ["healthcare",
# "global"]`` after the second MERGE. That re-introduced "global" alongside
# the specific sector and broke filtering / RAG semantics ("WHERE 'global'
# IN n.zone" started matching healthcare nodes).
#
# This helper builds the canonical "drop-global-if-specifics-exist"
# accumulator clause — one source of truth used by every node MERGE that
# accumulates zones. The CASE expression is small enough that re-evaluating
# the union twice is negligible vs the readability win.
def _zone_override_global_clause(node_var: str, source_expr: str, prop: str = "zone") -> str:
    """Return a Cypher SET-clause fragment that accumulates zones with the
    "specifics-override-global" rule applied at write time.

    Args:
        node_var: the bound node variable in the MERGE (e.g. ``"n"`` or ``"i"``), or (2026-10-16) the
            ``SOURCED_FROM`` relationship variable (``"r"``).
        source_expr: the Cypher expression yielding the new zones to merge in
            (e.g. ``"$zone"`` or ``"item.zone"``). Must already be a list.
        prop: the property that accumulates (``zone`` on a node; ``zones`` on a ``SOURCED_FROM`` edge,
            the zones one source's records gave the node, 2026-10-16).

    Returns:
        A string suitable for splicing into a ``SET ...`` clause, e.g.::

            f"SET {node_var}.score = 1, {_zone_override_global_clause('n', '$zone')}, ..."

    Result semantics (for any ingestion):
        - if union(existing, new) contains any sector other than 'global'
          → store only the specifics (drop 'global')
        - else (only 'global' or empty) → store the union as-is
    """
    # Validate the variable name to prevent Cypher injection via caller bug.
    # (Both inputs are constructed by EdgeGuard code, never by user input —
    # but a typo could still produce broken Cypher; better to fail loudly.)
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(node_var):
        raise ValueError(f"_zone_override_global_clause: invalid node_var {node_var!r}")
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(prop):
        raise ValueError(f"_zone_override_global_clause: invalid prop {prop!r}")
    # Route through the canonical dedup helper so the eventual native-Cypher
    # flip (Phase 3 of the apoc.coll.toSet migration plan) changes one function
    # instead of 47+ sites. The literal substring
    # "apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(n.zone, []) + $zone)" is still produced — see
    # ``_dedup_concat_clause`` and tests/test_pr33_bugbot_fixes.py:2430.
    union = _dedup_concat_clause(f"{node_var}.{prop}", source_expr)
    # PR-N19 Fix #2 (post-baseline 2026-04-22, from Bravo's baseline-run
    # audit): wrap the final zone expression in ``apoc.coll.sort`` to
    # guarantee canonical ordering across writes. Pre-PR-N19,
    # ``apoc.coll.toSet`` dedup'd exact-string entries but did NOT
    # sort, so two nodes seeing the same zones in different ingest
    # order produced different ``n.zone`` arrays:
    #   Node A: ["healthcare", "energy"]  (count=1)
    #   Node B: ["energy", "healthcare"]  (count=448)
    # ``MATCH (n) RETURN n.zone, count(n)`` groups by exact array
    # equality → fragmented sector stats + unstable STIX export
    # (any consumer hashing the zone array saw duplicate "sectors").
    #
    # Fix: canonical alphabetic sort at write time. Existing legacy
    # nodes can be repaired with one-shot Cypher migration:
    #   MATCH (n) WHERE n.zone IS NOT NULL
    #   SET n.zone = apoc.coll.sort(apoc.coll.toSet(n.zone))
    # documented in docs/RUNBOOK.md.
    return f"{node_var}.{prop} = {_zone_override_global_expr(union)}"


def _zone_override_global_expr(union: str) -> str:
    """The zones of the list expression ``union`` with the "specifics-override-global" rule, sorted: the
    right-hand side of ``_zone_override_global_clause`` (2026-10-16: also of a ``SOURCED_FROM`` edge's
    ``zones``, ``_sourced_zone_items``)."""
    specifics = f"[z IN {union} WHERE z <> 'global']"
    return f"CASE WHEN size({specifics}) > 0 THEN apoc.coll.sort({specifics}) ELSE apoc.coll.sort({union}) END"


def _sourced_zone_items(rel_var: str, zones_expr: str, stated_expr: str, stated_refs_expr: str) -> str:
    """``SET`` items of a ``SOURCED_FROM`` edge (2026-10-16): the zones this source's records gave the
    node (``zones``), the part of them the source stated itself (``stated_zones``,
    ``sector_evidence.stated_zones``) and which of the source's records stated which zone
    (``stated_refs``, ``"<zone>|<source ref>"``, ``sector_evidence.stated_refs``).

    ``zones`` accumulates with the node's rule (``global`` dropped once a sector is present, sorted),
    so ``build_relationships`` steps 7a-7d name on a link to a Sector only the feeds that gave that
    sector; a write without zones (``zones_expr`` null) leaves it as it is. ``stated_zones`` and
    ``stated_refs`` are written only when the record states a zone, as sorted sets that only grow; with
    ``stated_refs`` a sector link cites only the records that gave its sector, not every record of the
    source (a CVE that an ICS advisory names for Energy and a medical advisory for Healthcare). All three
    are read back by ``relationship_provenance.zone_prov_with``.
    """
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(rel_var):
        raise ValueError(f"_sourced_zone_items: invalid rel_var {rel_var!r}")
    zone_rule = _zone_override_global_expr(_dedup_concat_clause(f"{rel_var}.zones", zones_expr))

    def _growing_set(prop: str, expr: str) -> str:
        return (
            f"{rel_var}.{prop} = CASE WHEN size(coalesce({expr}, [])) = 0 THEN {rel_var}.{prop} "
            f"ELSE apoc.coll.sort({_dedup_concat_clause(f'{rel_var}.{prop}', expr)}) END"
        )

    return (
        f"{rel_var}.zones = CASE WHEN {zones_expr} IS NULL THEN {rel_var}.zones ELSE {zone_rule} END,\n"
        f"            {_growing_set('stated_zones', stated_expr)},\n"
        f"            {_growing_set('stated_refs', stated_refs_expr)}"
    )


def _unstated_sector_link_items(rel_var: str = "r") -> str:
    """``SET`` items of a link to a Sector written without a record of its own (2026-10-18,
    ``create_indicator_sector_relationship`` / ``create_vulnerability_sector_relationship``): the label and
    confidence ``$label`` / ``$confidence`` (``sector_evidence.link_evidence`` of no statement:
    ``zone_classification`` at the table's 0.5) by the batched writer's rule, so a stored stronger label and
    its confidence stay (an ``otx_industries`` or ``advisory_sector`` link was reset to 0.5 before)."""
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(rel_var):
        raise ValueError(f"_unstated_sector_link_items: invalid rel_var {rel_var!r}")
    r = rel_var
    return (
        f"{r}.match_type = CASE WHEN {r}.confidence_score IS NULL OR $confidence >= {r}.confidence_score "
        f"THEN $label ELSE {r}.match_type END,\n"
        f"            {r}.confidence_score = CASE WHEN {r}.confidence_score IS NULL OR $confidence > {r}.confidence_score "
        f"THEN $confidence ELSE {r}.confidence_score END"
    )


def _zone_param(zones: Any) -> Optional[List[str]]:
    """Zones, or ``stated_refs`` entries, as a parameter list (2026-10-16): ``None`` stays ``None``, a single
    string becomes a list."""
    if zones is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(zones, str):
        return [zones] if zones else []
    return [str(z) for z in zones if z is not None and str(z) != ""]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Canonical dedup-concat helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# The codebase has 47+ ``SET <prop> = apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(<prop>, []) + …)``
# fragments scattered across MERGE/SET clauses. Two problems:
#
#   1. ``apoc.coll.toSet`` is deprecated in Neo4j 2026.x (warns; will be
#      removed in a future major). When we eventually have to flip every
#      site to native Cypher, doing it in 47 places is a recipe for
#      partial-rollout bugs (a single missed site = silent unbounded list
#      growth, since Cypher does NOT auto-dedupe on SET despite a recent
#      reviewer claim to the contrary — verified, see the migration audit
#      in PR description).
#   2. There is currently no single place to instrument list sizes. The
#      worst-case lists in production (``n.misp_event_ids``,
#      ``r.misp_event_ids``) accumulate to 100–500+ entries on hot OTX
#      indicators across the 2-year baseline. We need observability before
#      we can decide whether the eventual replacement (``reduce()`` is
#      O(n²) and would add ~22 min to ``build_relationships`` at p99=500
#      per the perf audit; ``CASE WHEN $x IN coalesce(…)`` is O(n) but
#      semantically equivalent ONLY for append-of-one) is safe.
#
# These two helpers are the chokepoint for both concerns. Phase 2 of the
# migration (this PR): all 47+ sites route through these helpers, but the
# helpers internally still emit ``apoc.coll.toSet(...)`` — zero behavior
# change. Phase 3 (a follow-up PR, gated on the integration tests landed
# alongside these helpers): change ONLY the helper internals to native
# Cypher; every callsite picks up the new pattern automatically.
def _dedup_concat_clause(prop_ref: str, addition_expr: str) -> str:
    """Return the canonical Cypher fragment for dedup-concatenating *addition_expr* into *prop_ref*.

    Emits::

        apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(<prop_ref>, []) + <addition_expr>)

    Used by every list-accumulator SET clause that adds new elements to an
    existing list property (``n.source[]``, ``r.sources[]``, ``n.tags[]``,
    ``r.misp_event_ids[]``, …).

    Args:
        prop_ref: A dotted property reference of the form ``<var>.<name>``
            (e.g. ``"n.source"``, ``"r.sources"``). Both halves are validated
            with ``_PROP_NAME_RE`` to defend against Cypher-injection via
            caller bugs (the inputs are always constructed by EdgeGuard code,
            never from user input — this is belt-and-braces).
        addition_expr: ANY Cypher expression that evaluates to a list to
            merge into ``prop_ref``. Examples::

                "$source_array"
                "[$id]"
                "[item.tag]"
                "coalesce(item.tags, [])"

            Validation is the caller's responsibility; this helper just
            splices it verbatim.

    Returns:
        The set-union Cypher fragment, suitable for use as the right-hand
        side of a ``SET <prop_ref> = ...`` clause.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if ``prop_ref`` is not a well-formed ``<var>.<name>`` pair.
    """
    var, sep, name = prop_ref.partition(".")
    if not sep or not var or not name or "." in name:
        raise ValueError(f"_dedup_concat_clause: prop_ref must be of the form '<var>.<name>', got {prop_ref!r}")
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(var):
        raise ValueError(f"_dedup_concat_clause: invalid var {var!r} in prop_ref {prop_ref!r}")
    if not _PROP_NAME_RE.match(name):
        raise ValueError(f"_dedup_concat_clause: invalid prop name {name!r} in prop_ref {prop_ref!r}")
    return f"apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce({prop_ref}, []) + {addition_expr})"


def _tlp_rank_case(expr: str) -> str:
    """Cypher CASE ranking a TLP label (NULL / unknown → 0) so merges can keep the most restrictive."""
    return (
        f"CASE toLower(toString({expr})) WHEN 'red' THEN 5 WHEN 'amber+strict' THEN 4 WHEN 'amber' THEN 3 "
        f"WHEN 'green' THEN 2 WHEN 'white' THEN 1 WHEN 'clear' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END"
    )


def _tlp_most_restrictive_clause(existing: str, incoming: str) -> str:
    """2026-10 review fix: TLP is not last-writer-wins. If any source rated an entity
    ``amber`` it stays ``amber`` when an open feed (default ``white``) touches it next."""
    return f"CASE WHEN {_tlp_rank_case(incoming)} > {_tlp_rank_case(existing)} THEN {incoming} ELSE {existing} END"


def _set_if_absent_clause(existing: str, incoming: str) -> str:
    """2026-10: keep ``existing`` when it holds a value, else take ``incoming`` (an empty string
    counts as no value). For values a record may supply but must not replace: a CVE's dates from any
    record but NVD's (``_CVE_RECORD_DATE_PROPS``). A description follows the source ranking instead
    (``description_ranking``, 2026-10-16)."""
    return f"CASE WHEN {existing} IS NULL OR {existing} = '' THEN {incoming} ELSE {existing} END"


def _dedup_concat_optional_clause(
    prop_ref: str,
    value_expr: str,
    *,
    require_nonempty_string: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Return the dedup-concat fragment that appends ``value_expr`` only when non-null.

    Emits (with ``require_nonempty_string=False``)::

        apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(<prop_ref>, []) + CASE WHEN <value_expr> IS NOT NULL THEN [<value_expr>] ELSE [] END)

    Or, with ``require_nonempty_string=True``::

        apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(<prop_ref>, []) + CASE WHEN <value_expr> IS NOT NULL AND <value_expr> <> '' THEN [<value_expr>] ELSE [] END)

    This is the "Pattern B" CASE-gated variant used by every
    ``r.misp_event_ids`` / ``n.misp_event_ids`` SET clause where the
    incoming row may legitimately omit the field (UNWIND batch rows where
    not every row carries a MISP event id). Sharing one helper guarantees
    the gating predicate stays in lockstep across all 11 batch-relationship
    queries.

    Args:
        prop_ref: dotted property reference (see ``_dedup_concat_clause``).
        value_expr: scalar Cypher expression to append when the predicate
            holds (e.g. ``"row.misp_event_id"``, ``"$misp_event_id"``,
            ``"item.misp_attribute_id"``). Spliced verbatim into the
            predicate and the array-of-one literal — no validation.
        require_nonempty_string: if True, the predicate also requires
            ``value_expr <> ''``. The original batch-relationship templates
            in ``create_misp_relationships_batch`` used this guard for
            ``row.misp_event_id`` because some upstream paths produced
            empty strings rather than nulls; the node-side templates do
            not (those paths pre-filter to non-empty). Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        The set-union Cypher fragment as a single line (no embedded
        newlines), suitable for use as the right-hand side of a
        ``SET <prop_ref> = ...`` clause.
    """
    if require_nonempty_string:
        guard = f"{value_expr} IS NOT NULL AND {value_expr} <> ''"
    else:
        guard = f"{value_expr} IS NOT NULL"
    case_expr = f"CASE WHEN {guard} THEN [{value_expr}] ELSE [] END"
    return _dedup_concat_clause(prop_ref, case_expr)


def nonempty_graph_string(value: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Normalize a generic string used as a graph relationship endpoint (names, ids, values).

    Returns None for null, empty, or whitespace-only — callers must not create edges on unknowns.
    """
    if value is None:
        return None
    s = str(value).strip()
    return s if s else None


def _cve_cvss_selection_cypher(var: str = "c") -> str:
    """Cypher binding ``best`` to ``[sub-node, version]`` for the CVE in ``var``: its first CVSS
    sub-node, in the order of ``cvss_selection.CVSS_VERSIONS``, whose ``base_score`` is a number
    in [0, 10] (non-numeric or out-of-range values are skipped, like ``clamp_cvss_score``);
    ``best`` is null when the CVE has none."""
    candidates = ",\n            ".join(
        f"[head([({var})-[:{v.rel_type}]->(x:{v.label}) WHERE x.base_score >= 0.0 AND x.base_score <= 10.0 | x]), "
        f"'{v.version}']"
        for v in CVSS_VERSIONS
    )
    return f"WITH {var}, head([p IN [\n            {candidates}\n        ] WHERE p[0] IS NOT NULL]) AS best"


def _cve_severity_from_best_cypher() -> str:
    """Cypher expression for the rating of ``best`` (see ``_cve_cvss_selection_cypher``); mirrors
    ``cvss_selection.select_cvss``: the sub-node's own ``base_severity`` when it is a CVSS rating,
    else the rating of the score (NVD's CVSS 2 scale for version 2.0), ``UNKNOWN`` without CVSS."""
    ratings = ", ".join(f"'{s}'" for s in QUALITATIVE_SEVERITIES)
    stated = "toUpper(coalesce(toStringOrNull(best[0].base_severity), ''))"
    score = "best[0].base_score"
    return (
        f"CASE WHEN best IS NULL THEN '{UNKNOWN_SEVERITY}' "
        f"WHEN {stated} IN [{ratings}] THEN {stated} "
        f"WHEN best[1] = '2.0' THEN CASE WHEN {score} >= 7.0 THEN 'HIGH' WHEN {score} >= 4.0 THEN 'MEDIUM' ELSE 'LOW' END "
        f"WHEN {score} = 0.0 THEN 'NONE' WHEN {score} >= 9.0 THEN 'CRITICAL' WHEN {score} >= 7.0 THEN 'HIGH' "
        f"WHEN {score} >= 4.0 THEN 'MEDIUM' ELSE 'LOW' END"
    )


def _attack_vector_word_cypher(expr: str) -> str:
    """Cypher expression for NVD's word of the attack-vector spelling in ``expr``
    (``cvss_selection.ATTACK_VECTOR_SPELLINGS``, any case); null for any other value."""
    whens = " ".join(f"WHEN '{spelling}' THEN '{word}'" for spelling, word in ATTACK_VECTOR_SPELLINGS.items())
    return f"CASE toUpper(trim(toStringOrNull({expr}))) {whens} ELSE null END"


def _cve_attack_vector_from_best_cypher() -> str:
    """Cypher expression for the attack vector of ``best`` (see ``_cve_cvss_selection_cypher``);
    mirrors ``cvss_selection.payload_attack_vector``: the field of best's version (``attack_vector``
    of CVSS 3.x, ``access_vector`` of CVSS 2), else the ``AV`` metric of its ``vector_string`` (a
    CVSS 4.0 sub-node stores only the vector string), as NVD's word; null without CVSS."""
    fields = " ".join(f"WHEN '{v.version}' THEN best[0].{v.vector_field}" for v in CVSS_VERSIONS if v.vector_field)
    stated = _attack_vector_word_cypher(f"CASE best[1] {fields} END")
    metric = (
        "head([m IN split(trim(toStringOrNull(best[0].vector_string)), '/') "
        "WHERE m STARTS WITH 'AV:' | substring(m, 3)])"
    )
    return f"CASE WHEN best IS NULL THEN null ELSE coalesce({stated}, {_attack_vector_word_cypher(metric)}) END"


# 2026-10: a CVE node's ``cvss_score`` / ``severity`` / ``cvss_version`` / ``attack_vector`` come
# from its CVSS sub-nodes, never from the record being merged (see ``cvss_selection``). Derived
# after every ``merge_cve``, so the result does not depend on which source's record arrives last,
# and a CVE without CVSS loses any score or attack vector an older run stored (null score and
# attack vector, severity UNKNOWN).
_CVE_SCORE_FROM_CVSS_QUERY = (
    "MATCH (c:CVE {cve_id: $cve_id})\n"
    f"{_cve_cvss_selection_cypher('c')}\n"
    "SET c.cvss_score = best[0].base_score,\n"
    "    c.cvss_version = best[1],\n"
    f"    c.severity = {_cve_severity_from_best_cypher()},\n"
    f"    c.attack_vector = {_cve_attack_vector_from_best_cypher()}"
)

# the record's key -> (node property, allowed values; None = a bounded string).
_NVD_SSVC_PROPERTIES: Dict[str, Tuple[str, Optional[FrozenSet[str]]]] = {
    "exploitation": ("ssvc_exploitation", frozenset({"none", "poc", "active"})),
    "automatable": ("ssvc_automatable", frozenset({"yes", "no"})),
    "technical_impact": ("ssvc_technical_impact", frozenset({"partial", "total"})),
    "version": ("ssvc_version", None),
    "timestamp": ("ssvc_timestamp", None),
}


def _nvd_ssvc_values(ssvc: Any) -> Dict[str, Optional[str]]:
    """The SSVC node properties of an NVD record's ``ssvc`` (validated; None removes a property).

    MISP is an input boundary, so a value outside the allowed set, a non-string or an overlong
    string is dropped. Without any decision point the record has no SSVC and every property is None.
    """
    values: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {prop: None for prop, _ in _NVD_SSVC_PROPERTIES.values()}
    if not isinstance(ssvc, dict):
        return values
    for key, (prop, allowed) in _NVD_SSVC_PROPERTIES.items():
        value = ssvc.get(key)
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip() or len(value) > 64:
            continue
        value = value.strip().lower() if allowed is not None else value.strip()
        if allowed is None or value in allowed:
            values[prop] = value
    if not any(values[_NVD_SSVC_PROPERTIES[k][0]] for k in ("exploitation", "automatable", "technical_impact")):
        return {prop: None for prop in values}
    return values


def clamp_confidence_score(value: Any) -> Optional[float]:
    """PR-N14 (pre-baseline audit Fix #2, 2026-04-21): clamp
    confidence_score to [0.0, 1.0] + reject non-finite.

    Pre-PR-N14, the max-wins CASE in every ``_upsert_sourced_relationship``
    and batched UNWIND happily accepted ``$confidence = inf`` from a
    compromised feed and pinned ``r.confidence_score = Infinity``
    forever, corrupting every query that sorts or filters on
    confidence.

    Returns None for unparseable / non-finite / out-of-range so callers
    can fall back to the documented default (0.5 at most sites).
    """
    import math

    if value is None:
        return None
    try:
        f = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not math.isfinite(f):
        return None
    if f < 0.0 or f > 1.0:
        return None
    return f


def _clamp_confidence_with_log(raw: Any, label: str, source_id: str, default: float = 0.5) -> float:
    """PR-N14 follow-up (cursor-bugbot 2026-04-21 Medium):
    single evaluation of ``clamp_confidence_score`` + WARN-on-reject,
    so the batch paths in ``merge_indicators_batch`` and
    ``merge_vulnerabilities_batch`` don't (a) call the clamp twice per
    row in the hot loop, and (b) silently swallow rejects — the
    single-item ``merge_node_with_source`` path emits a WARN and the
    batch paths MUST emit the same signal so operators can identify
    the offending feed uniformly.

    Returns ``clamped`` on success, ``default`` (0.5) on reject.
    Never returns None — callers use the return value as a Cypher
    param.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return default
    clamped = clamp_confidence_score(raw)
    if clamped is None:
        logger.warning(
            "confidence_score rejected by clamp for %s/%s (claimed=%r) — falling back to %.2f. Compromised feed?",
            label,
            source_id,
            raw,
            default,
        )
        return default
    return clamped


def normalize_cve_id_for_graph(value: Any) -> Optional[str]:

    Never returns blank/whitespace — callers must not MERGE or link on null/empty data.

    s = nonempty_graph_string(value)

def resolve_vulnerability_cve_id(item: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Resolve CVE identifier for Vulnerability MERGE keys and cross-item relationships.

    MISP vulnerability attributes often carry the CVE only in ``value``; some ingestion
    paths omit ``cve_id``. Returns an uppercase string (e.g. CVE-2025-32432) or None.

    cid = normalize_cve_id_for_graph(item.get("cve_id"))

# ``merge_vulnerabilities_batch``, ``link_to_source``) MATCH the ``Source`` node and never create

# alias (``otx``, ``cisa``, ``feodo``, ``sslbl``, ...) writes to the canonical node, and an id the
# registry does not know matches no node (the batch writers refuse it).
SOURCES = source_registry.to_neo4j_sources_dict()


def _canonical_source_list(names: Any) -> List[str]:
    """A node's ``source`` list as the writers store it: each name resolved with
    ``source_registry.canonical_source_id`` (a variant to its canonical id; a name the registry does
    not know lowercased and stripped, as in ``r.sources``), blanks dropped, duplicates removed in
    order. A single string counts as a one-item list. The REST ``source`` filter resolves its value
    the same way, so ``otx`` finds the nodes whose list holds ``alienvault_otx``."""
    if isinstance(names, str):
        names = [names]
    out: List[str] = []
    for name in names or ():
        sid = source_registry.canonical_source_id(name)
        if sid and sid not in out:
            out.append(sid)
    return out


# PR-N15 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit Fix #1): Neo4j error codes that
# the server reports as TransientError OR as DatabaseError-wrapped
# transient conditions. The driver classifies most `Neo.TransientError.*`
# into the ``neo4j_exceptions.TransientError`` Python class, BUT some
# deadlock / lock-acquisition scenarios surface as
# ``neo4j_exceptions.DatabaseError`` with a Neo.TransientError.* code,
# because the server wraps the transient error into
# ``Neo.DatabaseError.Statement.ExecutionFailed``.
#
# Pre-PR-N15, every ``DatabaseError`` was treated as terminal (returned
# ``[]`` in ``run()``; counted as error_count in merge batches). Those
# write paths silently dropped rows on every Neo4j GC pause >5s or
# concurrent writer deadlock. Post-PR-N15 the decorator below matches
# on ``.code`` substrings so the retry path catches them.
#
# Reference: https://neo4j.com/docs/status-codes/current/errors/
_RETRYABLE_NEO4J_CODE_SUBSTRINGS = (
    "Neo.TransientError",  # Any transient — lock timeout, deadlock, memory pool exhausted
    "Neo.ClientError.Transaction.DeadlockDetected",  # Some drivers surface as ClientError
    "Transaction.LockClientStopped",
    "Transaction.LockAcquisitionTimeout",
    "Transaction.Terminated",
    "General.DatabaseUnavailable",
    "Cluster.NotALeader",
)


def _is_retryable_neo4j_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
    """PR-N15 Fix #1: classify a Neo4j exception as retryable or
    terminal by inspecting its ``.code`` attribute.

    Returns True for retryable conditions (deadlocks, lock-acquisition
    timeouts, cluster failover, temporary memory exhaustion). False
    for truly terminal errors (schema / constraint / syntax).

    Used by the retry decorator AND by the merge-batch exception
    handlers — same classification both places so the retry decision
    is consistent across layers.
    """
    # Transient classes are always retryable.
    if isinstance(exc, (neo4j_exceptions.ServiceUnavailable, neo4j_exceptions.TransientError)):
        return True
    if isinstance(exc, (ConnectionError, TimeoutError)):
        return True
    # DatabaseError / ClientError subclasses: inspect the .code attribute.
    code = getattr(exc, "code", None) or ""
    if not code:
        return False
    for marker in _RETRYABLE_NEO4J_CODE_SUBSTRINGS:
        if marker in code:
            return True
    return False


def retry_with_backoff(max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES, base_delay: float = RETRY_DELAY_BASE):
    """Decorator for retry logic with exponential backoff.

    PR-N15 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit Fix #1): also retries
    ``DatabaseError``-wrapped transient errors via the
    ``_is_retryable_neo4j_error`` classifier. Pre-PR-N15 a
    ``Neo.DatabaseError.Statement.ExecutionFailed`` wrapping a deadlock
    hit the generic ``except Exception`` and re-raised as terminal —
    no retry, caller saw a failure it should have retried.

    TODO (post-baseline, tracked in the 7-agent audit's "execute_write
    migration" item): every write path in this module uses the
    auto-commit ``session.run`` API. Neo4j's official Python driver
    recommends the ``session.execute_write`` managed-transaction API
    for mutating queries — it provides AUTOMATIC retry on transient
    errors + atomic rollback on mid-statement failure. This decorator
    partially closes the gap (retry) but does NOT give atomicity —
    an exception mid-UNWIND can commit partial state. Full migration
    is ~40 call sites; deferred
    pending post-baseline stability validation. Not a baseline
    blocker because the batched paths (``merge_indicators_batch``,
    ``merge_vulnerabilities_batch``, ``_execute_batch_with_retry``,
    ``_run_rows``) now retry and PR-N9 B6 + PR-N15 permanent-failure
    counter detect silent-write failures. But for max safety the
    ``execute_write`` migration should land in a post-baseline PR.
    """

    def decorator(func):
        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            last_exception = None
            for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):  # +1: first attempt + max_retries retries (matches collector_utils)
                try:
                    return func(*args, **kwargs)
                except Exception as e:
                    # PR-N15: classify retryable vs terminal uniformly
                    # via ``_is_retryable_neo4j_error``. Covers
                    # ServiceUnavailable / TransientError / ConnectionError /
                    # TimeoutError (pre-PR-N15 behaviour) AND
                    # DatabaseError-wrapped transient errors via .code
                    # inspection (new in PR-N15).
                    if _is_retryable_neo4j_error(e):
                        last_exception = e
                        if attempt >= max_retries:
                            break  # exhausted all retries
                        delay = base_delay * (2**attempt)
                        code = getattr(e, "code", "")
                        logger.warning(
                            f"{func.__name__} failed (attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries + 1}): "
                            f"{type(e).__name__}{f' [{code}]' if code else ''}: {e}. "
                            f"Retrying in {delay}s..."
                        )
                        time.sleep(delay)
                        continue
                    # Non-retryable.
                    logger.error(f"{func.__name__} failed with non-retryable error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
                    raise

            logger.error(f"{func.__name__} failed after {max_retries + 1} attempts")
            raise last_exception

        return wrapper

    return decorator

def _cvss_legacy_sources_cypher(node: str) -> str:
    """2026-10: the feeds a ``HAS_CVSS_*`` edge without ``sources`` (written before relationship
    provenance) counts as asserted by: the CVSS sub-node's ``tag``, the feed that first wrote it, named as
    ``Neo4jClient._merge_cvss_node`` names a feed (``default``, the tag of an item without one, is
    ``misp``); none when the sub-node has no tag. ``_merge_cvss_node`` reads it in its NVD guard and seeds
    such an edge's ``sources`` with it before adding its own feed, so a later write still sees that feed."""
    return (
        f"CASE WHEN {node}.tag IS NULL OR {node}.tag = '' THEN [] "
        f"WHEN {node}.tag = 'default' THEN ['misp'] ELSE [{node}.tag] END"
    )


def _cve_sub_write_failed(exc: Exception, what: str) -> bool:
    """The error handling of ``merge_cve``'s sub-writes: the CVSS sub-nodes, the NVD-owned data and
    the CVE score (2026-10). A retryable error (``_is_retryable_neo4j_error``) is raised again, so the
    method's ``@retry_with_backoff`` retries it and raises it once the retries are spent, as for
    ``merge_node_with_source``; a terminal error is logged at ERROR and returned as False, which
    ``merge_cve`` returns, so the sync counts the CVE as an error. Until 2026-10 these writes logged
    every error at WARNING, retryable ones included, and the CVE counted as synced."""
    if _is_retryable_neo4j_error(exc):
        raise exc
    logger.error("%s (terminal): %s: %s", what, type(exc).__name__, exc)
    return False


def _alert_default_tlp() -> str:

# 2026-10 shared-database contract. ``edgeguard_managed = true`` means EdgeGuard CREATED the
# node, so every node MERGE stamps it on the create path only. When EdgeGuard writes onto a node
# another system created first (ResilMesh topology, a CRUSOE scanner's CVE / Vulnerability), the
# MATCH path stamps ``edgeguard_enriched = true`` instead. ``clear_edgeguard_managed`` deletes the
# first set and never the second; the REST / GraphQL / STIX readers expose both. The clause is
# spliced literally into each query (same convention as ``indicator_aging``); this helper is
# the single definition the tests compare every splice against.
def _enriched_on_match_clause(var: str) -> str:
    """``ON MATCH`` sub-clause marking a node EdgeGuard wrote to but did not create."""
    return (
        f"ON MATCH SET {var}.edgeguard_enriched = CASE WHEN {var}.edgeguard_managed = true "
        f"THEN {var}.edgeguard_enriched ELSE true END"
    )
