# legitimately there (the same SoftwareVersion.version per product, the same NetworkService
# port/protocol per host, …); CRUSOE's own client refuses a UNIQUE on SoftwareVersion.version.
# A constraint created by EdgeGuard made the partner's scanner writes fail with
# ConstraintValidationFailed. ``node_identity._NATURAL_KEYS`` still defines their deterministic
# uuid; ``create_constraints`` drops any instance an older EdgeGuard build created.
SHARED_LABELS_WITHOUT_UNIQUE_CONSTRAINT = frozenset(
    {"Device", "NetworkService", "SoftwareVersion", "Application", "Role", "User"}
)


def _normalise_zone_list(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """``Alert.zone`` is a list of EdgeGuard zone names, like every other ``zone`` property.

    Accepts the scalar NATS form, lower-cases and strips each entry, keeps only names in
    ``config.VALID_ZONES`` (a partner's unknown or mis-cased sector strings are logged and
    dropped, never stored) and falls back to ``["global"]`` so an alert never lacks a zone.
    """
    from config import VALID_ZONES  # local import: config needs the runtime environment

    if isinstance(value, str):
        items = [value]
    elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set)):
        items = list(value)
    else:
        items = []
    cleaned: List[str] = []
    unknown: List[str] = []
    for raw in items:
        if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
            continue
        name = raw.strip().lower()
        if name not in VALID_ZONES:
            unknown.append(name)
        elif name not in cleaned:
            cleaned.append(name)
    if unknown:
        # Partner-supplied strings: strip line breaks before logging (log injection) and log at
        # DEBUG, as the project rule for zone parameters requires.
        shown = ", ".join(sorted(set(unknown)))[:200].replace("\n", " ").replace("\r", " ")
        logger.debug("Alert zone(s) outside EdgeGuard's vocabulary dropped: %s", shown)
    return cleaned or ["global"]


# 2026-10-16: lifecycle writes by label (``indicator_aging``). Before, every node write reactivated
# a decay-retired node (``active = true``, ``retired_at`` / ``retired_by`` cleared,
# ``last_decayed_tier = null``) whatever its label and restored a decayed confidence by max-wins, so
# a full sync undid the decay. Now only an Indicator ages: its writes record the report
# (``indicator_aging.node_report_items``), then apply the one rule in a SET clause of its own
# (``indicator_aging.aging_set_clause``) at the database's current time, lifted to the node's
# ``aging_evaluated_at`` when that is later; it reactivates a node only when a newer report moves its
# basis. The batch and single-item writes read the node for the rule after a clause that set its
# properties, under the node's write lock; the alert path applies the rule in a second statement of
# its transaction (``create_indicator_from_alert``). Every other label is set ``active = true`` when
# EdgeGuard creates it (``_create_active``) and gets no ``active``, ``retired_*`` or decay property
# when EdgeGuard matches it, so a node another system created (CASM CVE / CVSS, ISIM assets) never
# receives an EdgeGuard lifecycle property and a manual decommission is never touched.
def _create_active(var: str) -> str:
    """``ON CREATE`` item of a node that does not age: active from its creation, never changed by a
    later EdgeGuard write."""
    return f"{var}.active = true"


def _statement_head(query: Any) -> str:
    """The first characters of a Cypher statement, whitespace collapsed, for a log line."""
    text = getattr(query, "text", query)
    return " ".join(str(text).split())[:160]


def _log_if_timed_out(exc: BaseException, timeout: Optional[float], statement: str) -> None:
    """Log once when ``exc`` is the server aborting a statement at its transaction timeout (2026-10).

    The driver raises the error when the result is read, so the statement and its limit are named
    here: without this line the task log carried only the server's generic termination message.
    """
    code = str(getattr(exc, "code", "") or "")
    if "TransactionTimedOut" not in code or getattr(exc, "_edgeguard_timeout_logged", False):
        return
    try:
        exc._edgeguard_timeout_logged = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    except Exception:  # an exception type without a __dict__ is logged every time it passes
        pass
    if timeout is not None and timeout == float(NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT):
        setting = "EDGEGUARD_NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT; raise it if the statement is expected to run longer"
    elif timeout is not None and timeout == float(_REL_QUERY_TIMEOUT):
        setting = "the relationship-batch limit (_REL_QUERY_TIMEOUT in src/neo4j_client.py)"
    else:
        setting = "the limit its caller sets (REST and STIX queries: 300 s)"
    logger.error(
        "[NEO4J-TIMEOUT] the server aborted a statement at its %s s transaction timeout: %s — set by %s",
        f"{timeout:.0f}" if timeout is not None else "?",
        statement,
        setting,
    )


class _TimeoutResult:
    """Result proxy: a timeout raised while the result is read is logged (``_log_if_timed_out``)."""

    __slots__ = ("_inner", "_timeout", "_statement")

    def __init__(self, inner: Any, timeout: float, statement: str) -> None:
        self._inner = inner
        self._timeout = timeout
        self._statement = statement

    def __iter__(self) -> Any:
        try:
            yield from self._inner
        except Exception as e:
            _log_if_timed_out(e, self._timeout, self._statement)
            raise

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
        attr = getattr(self._inner, name)
        if not callable(attr):
            return attr

        def _call(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            try:
                return attr(*args, **kwargs)
            except Exception as e:
                _log_if_timed_out(e, self._timeout, self._statement)
                raise

        return _call


class _TimeoutSession:
    """Session proxy: a ``timeout=`` keyword on ``run()`` becomes a real transaction timeout.

    2026-10 production-readiness check: the neo4j 5 driver merges unknown ``run()`` keywords into
    the Cypher parameters, so every ``session.run(q, timeout=30)`` in this code base sent a
    ``$timeout`` parameter and enforced nothing — a stalled statement ran until Airflow's task
    timeout. Wrapping the statement in ``neo4j.Query(text, timeout=…)`` makes the server abort
    the auto-commit transaction after that many seconds (``TransactionTimedOut``), which the retry
    classifier and the circuit breaker then see. Every other attribute is delegated unchanged.
    """

    __slots__ = ("_inner", "_cm", "_last")

    def __init__(self, session: Any) -> None:
        self._inner = session
        self._cm: Any = None
        self._last: Optional[Tuple[float, str]] = None  # (timeout, statement) of the last timed statement

    def run(self, query: Any, parameters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, *, timeout: Any = None, **kwargs: Any):
        if timeout is not None and isinstance(query, str):
            query = Query(query, timeout=float(timeout))
        if timeout is None:
            return self._inner.run(query, parameters, **kwargs)
        statement = _statement_head(query)
        # Not a call site: the timeout now travels inside the Query object (see the module's
        # scan test, which requires ``timeout=`` on every real ``session.run`` caller).
        try:
            result = self._inner.run(query, parameters, **kwargs)
        except Exception as e:
            # The driver reads an unread earlier result before it runs the next statement, so a
            # timeout raised here belongs to the previous statement when there is one.
            _log_if_timed_out(e, *(self._last or (float(timeout), statement)))
            raise
        self._last = (float(timeout), statement)
        return _TimeoutResult(result, float(timeout), statement)

    def __enter__(self) -> "_TimeoutSession":
        # Delegate to whatever the inner context manager yields (a real Session yields itself;
        # test doubles may yield another object) and remember the manager for __exit__.
        self._cm = self._inner
        entered = self._cm.__enter__()
        if entered is not None:
            self._inner = entered
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: Any) -> Any:
        manager = self._cm if self._cm is not None else self._inner
        self._cm = None
        try:
            return manager.__exit__(*exc)
        except Exception as e:
            # A session whose close raises (a test double, a future driver). The neo4j 5 driver's
            # Session.close reads a result left unread and logs its error as a WARNING without
            # raising it (2026-10-16), so every write here reads its result (``.consume()``,
            # ``.single()``, iteration) inside the caller's ``try``, where retry and error counting
            # see the error and ``_TimeoutResult`` logs a timeout.
            if self._last is not None:
                _log_if_timed_out(e, *self._last)
            raise

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
        return getattr(self._inner, name)


def _configured_database() -> Optional[str]:
    """``NEO4J_DATABASE`` when set and non-empty, else None (the server's default database).

    ``config.NEO4J_DATABASE`` was read but never passed to a session, so the variable had no
    effect; only an explicit value is forwarded, which keeps single-database servers unchanged.
    """
    return (os.getenv("NEO4J_DATABASE") or "").strip() or None


def session_kwargs() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Keyword arguments for a raw ``driver.session(...)`` call outside this client (CLI checks,
    version probe): ``{"database": <name>}`` when ``NEO4J_DATABASE`` is set, else empty, so every
    session of the deployment targets the same database."""
    database = _configured_database()
    return {"database": database} if database else {}


class _TimeoutDriver:
    """Driver proxy whose sessions translate ``timeout=`` into transaction timeouts (see above)
    and target the configured database when ``NEO4J_DATABASE`` is set."""

    __slots__ = ("_raw", "_database")

    def __init__(self, driver: Any, database: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        self._raw = driver
        self._database = database

    def session(self, **kwargs: Any) -> _TimeoutSession:
        if self._database and "database" not in kwargs:
            kwargs["database"] = self._database
        return _TimeoutSession(self._raw.session(**kwargs))

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
        return getattr(self._raw, name)


class Neo4jClient:
    """Production-ready Neo4j client with retry logic and batch processing."""

    def __init__(self, uri: str = None, user: str = None, password: str = None):
        from config import NEO4J_PASSWORD, NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER

        self.uri = uri or NEO4J_URI
        self.user = user or NEO4J_USER
        self.password = password or NEO4J_PASSWORD
        self.driver = None
        self._connection_healthy = False

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=MAX_RETRIES)
    def connect(self) -> bool:
        """
        Connect to Neo4j with retry logic.

        Returns:
            True if connection successful, False otherwise
        """
        try:
            logger.info(f"Connecting to Neo4j at {self.uri}")
            # _TimeoutDriver: every ``session.run(..., timeout=)`` in this code base becomes a real
            # server-side transaction timeout (see the proxy classes above).
            self.driver = _TimeoutDriver(
                GraphDatabase.driver(
                    self.uri,
                    auth=(self.user, self.password),
                    connection_timeout=NEO4J_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT,
                    max_connection_lifetime=3600,
                    max_connection_pool_size=50,
                    connection_acquisition_timeout=120,
                    # The server flags apoc.coll.toSet / apoc.coll.sort as deprecated and the driver
                    # logs each notice at WARNING with the full query text: one sync wrote a 5.4 GB
                    # task log. Other notification categories still arrive.
                    notifications_disabled_categories=[NotificationDisabledCategory.DEPRECATION],
                ),
                database=_configured_database(),
            )

            # Verify connection with health check
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                result = session.run("RETURN 1 as test", timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT)
                result.single()

            self._connection_healthy = True
            logger.info("Connected to Neo4j successfully")
            return True

        except neo4j_exceptions.AuthError as e:
            logger.error(f"Neo4j authentication failed: {e}")
            self._connection_healthy = False
            # PR-A audit fix (Bug Hunter HIGH H1): close + null-out the driver
            # before returning. ``self.driver = GraphDatabase.driver(...)`` at
            # line 435 ALREADY assigned a live driver before the verify
            # ``session.run`` raised. Returning False without closing leaks the
            # driver's connection pool. Operationally certain to bite during
            # MISP password rotation: every retry creates a fresh driver,
            # exhausting fds within the 5h baseline timeout.
            self._safe_close_driver()
            return False
        except (
            neo4j_exceptions.ServiceUnavailable,
            neo4j_exceptions.TransientError,
            ConnectionError,
            TimeoutError,
        ):
            self._connection_healthy = False
            # Same leak shape as AuthError above — even though the retry
            # decorator will re-call ``connect()`` and overwrite ``self.driver``,
            # the previous driver instance leaks unless we explicitly close it
            # here before re-raising.
            self._safe_close_driver()
            raise  # let @retry_with_backoff handle transient errors
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Neo4j connection failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            self._connection_healthy = False
            self._safe_close_driver()
            return False

    def _safe_close_driver(self) -> None:
        """Close the driver if alive and null it out. No-raise.

        Used by ``connect()``'s exception branches (PR-A audit fix; Bug Hunter
        HIGH H1). The neo4j-python-driver's ``Driver.close()`` is idempotent
        but can raise on a half-initialised driver, so we wrap defensively.
        """
        drv = self.driver
        self.driver = None  # null first so a re-call to connect() doesn't see a half-closed driver
        if drv is None:
            return
        try:
            drv.close()
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover — defensive
            logger.debug("Best-effort close on failed-connect driver raised: %s", exc)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close connection safely."""
        if self.driver:
            try:
                self.driver.close()
                logger.info("Neo4j connection closed")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Error closing Neo4j connection: {e}")
            finally:
                self.driver = None
                self._connection_healthy = False

    def is_connected(self) -> bool:
        """True if a Bolt driver was created (after :meth:`connect`).

        This is a **fast** check for API request guards; it does not ping the
        server. Use :meth:`health_check` for liveness + APOC validation.
        """
        return self.driver is not None

    def health_check(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Perform health check on Neo4j connection.

        Returns:
            Dict with health status information
        """
        if not self.driver:
            return {"healthy": False, "error": "No driver initialized"}

        try:
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                start_time = time.time()
                result = session.run("RETURN 1 as test", timeout=10)
                result.single()
                response_time = time.time() - start_time

                # Get database info
                db_info = session.run(
                    "CALL dbms.components() YIELD name, versions, edition RETURN name, versions, edition",
                    timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
                )
                db_record = db_info.single()

                base = {
                    "healthy": True,
                    "response_time_ms": round(response_time * 1000, 2),
                    "database": db_record["name"] if db_record else "unknown",
                    "version": db_record["versions"][0] if db_record and db_record["versions"] else "unknown",
                    "edition": db_record["edition"] if db_record else "unknown",
                }

                # APOC is required for MERGE list deduplication (apoc.coll.toSet) and sector labels.
                try:
                    apoc_test = session.run("RETURN size(apoc.coll.toSet([1, 2, 2])) AS n", timeout=10)
                    row = apoc_test.single()
                    if row is None or row["n"] != 2:
                        raise RuntimeError("APOC apoc.coll.toSet returned unexpected result")
                    base["apoc_available"] = True
                except Exception as apoc_err:
                    logger.error(f"Neo4j APOC check failed (sync will not work): {apoc_err}")
                    return {
                        "healthy": False,
                        "error": (
                            "Neo4j APOC plugin is missing or not allowed. "
                            "EdgeGuard requires APOC (e.g. docker-compose: NEO4J_PLUGINS='[\"apoc\"]' "
                            "and dbms.security.procedures allowlist for apoc.*). "
                            f"Details: {apoc_err}"
                        ),
                        "apoc_available": False,
                    }

                return base
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Health check failed: {e}")
            return {"healthy": False, "error": str(e)}

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def run(self, query: str, parameters: Dict = None, timeout: int = None) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Run a generic query with retry logic.

        Args:
            query: Cypher query string
            parameters: Query parameters
            timeout: Query timeout in seconds

        Returns:
            List of result records
        """
        if not self.driver:
            logger.error("Cannot run query: no connection to Neo4j")
            return []

        timeout = timeout or NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT
        parameters = parameters or {}

        _t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                result = session.run(query, parameters, timeout=timeout)
                records = [dict(record) for record in result]
            if _METRICS_AVAILABLE:
                NEO4J_QUERIES.labels(query_type="cypher", status="success").inc()
                NEO4J_QUERY_DURATION.labels(query_type="cypher").observe(time.monotonic() - _t0)
            return records
        except neo4j_exceptions.CypherSyntaxError as e:
            if _METRICS_AVAILABLE:
                NEO4J_QUERIES.labels(query_type="cypher", status="error").inc()
            logger.error(f"Cypher syntax error: {e}")
            return []
        except (
            neo4j_exceptions.ServiceUnavailable,
            neo4j_exceptions.TransientError,
            ConnectionError,
            TimeoutError,
        ):
            if _METRICS_AVAILABLE:
                NEO4J_QUERIES.labels(query_type="cypher", status="error").inc()
            raise  # let @retry_with_backoff handle transient errors
        except neo4j_exceptions.DatabaseError as e:
            # PR-N15 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit Fix #1): distinguish
            # retryable DatabaseError subtypes from terminal ones via
            # the shared ``_is_retryable_neo4j_error`` classifier. Pre-
            # PR-N15, every DatabaseError was swallowed (returned ``[]``)
            # — including ``Neo.DatabaseError.Statement.ExecutionFailed``
            # which wraps deadlocks and lock-acquisition timeouts. At
            # 730d baseline scale with concurrent build_relationships
            # and enrichment writers, that silent-zero-edge pattern was
            # guaranteed to fire (same class as PR-N7 deadlock-bug but
            # in a different layer). Retryable → re-raise so the
            # decorator retries; terminal → return [] (schema / constraint
            # / syntax are never fixed by retrying).
            if _METRICS_AVAILABLE:
                NEO4J_QUERIES.labels(query_type="cypher", status="error").inc()
            if _is_retryable_neo4j_error(e):
                code = getattr(e, "code", "")
                logger.warning(
                    "Neo4j DatabaseError classified as retryable (code=%r); re-raising for retry decorator. Error: %s",
                    code,
                    e,
                )
                raise
            logger.error(f"Neo4j database error (terminal): {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            return []

    # Node batch of ``clear_all`` and ``clear_edgeguard_managed``; their relationships go first, in
    # batches of 50,000 (``_delete_relationships_batched``).
    _CLEAR_NODE_BATCH = 10_000

    @staticmethod
    def _delete_relationships_batched(
        session, match_clause: str, batch_size: int = 50_000, progress: Optional[_ClearProgress] = None
    ) -> int:
        """Delete the relationships selected by ``match_clause`` (which binds ``r``) in
        batches of ``batch_size`` until a batch deletes nothing. Returns the total; ``progress``
        counts each batch as it commits, so a clear that fails later still knows what went.

        Deleting relationships ahead of the node batches keeps each transaction's
        working set bounded by ``batch_size`` edges instead of by the degree of
        whatever nodes land in a ``DETACH DELETE`` batch. On the 2026-09 graph
        (478K nodes, 2.66M relationships) the first 10,000-node batch held hubs
        (Source, Tactic, popular Malware) and ran a 2g heap out of memory
        (``Neo.TransientError.General.OutOfMemoryError``, 2026-10-12).
        """
        total = 0
        while True:
            result = session.run(
                f"{match_clause} WITH DISTINCT r LIMIT {batch_size} DELETE r RETURN count(r) AS deleted",
                timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
            )
            batch_deleted = result.single()["deleted"]
            if not batch_deleted:
                return total
            total += batch_deleted
            if progress is not None:
                progress.relationships += batch_deleted
            logger.debug(f"Deleted batch of {batch_deleted} relationships")

    @staticmethod
    def _record_failed_clear(
        operation: str,
        scope: str,
        progress: _ClearProgress,
        exc: BaseException,
        details: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Audit line of a clear attempt that failed after deleting something (2026-10-23).

        ``affected`` is the nodes this attempt deleted before ``exc``; ``details`` adds the
        relationships it deleted, ``outcome = "failed"`` and the error's type. An attempt that
        deleted nothing writes no line. ``@retry_with_backoff`` runs a clear again after a
        transient error and each attempt writes its own line, so the lines of one run add up to
        what it deleted.
        """
        if not (progress.nodes or progress.relationships):
            return
        record_destructive_op(
            operation,
            target="neo4j",
            affected=progress.nodes,
            scope=scope,
            details={
                **(details or {}),
                "relationships_deleted": progress.relationships,
                "outcome": "failed",
                "error": type(exc).__name__,
            },
        )

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def clear_all(self) -> bool:
        """
        Clear all nodes and relationships safely.

        Returns:
            True if successful, False otherwise
        """
        if not self.driver:
            logger.error("Cannot clear: no connection to Neo4j")
            return False

        progress = _ClearProgress()
        try:
            logger.warning("Clearing all nodes and relationships from Neo4j...")
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                # Get counts before clearing
                counts = session.run("MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) as count", timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT)
                node_count = counts.single()["count"]

                # Relationships first, in bounded batches (see _delete_relationships_batched).
                self._delete_relationships_batched(session, "MATCH ()-[r]->()", progress=progress)

                # Clear in batches to avoid memory issues
                while progress.nodes < node_count:
                    result = session.run(
                        f"MATCH (n) WITH n LIMIT {self._CLEAR_NODE_BATCH} DETACH DELETE n RETURN count(n) as deleted",
                        timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
                    )
                    batch_deleted = result.single()["deleted"]
                    if batch_deleted == 0:
                        break
                    progress.nodes += batch_deleted
                    logger.debug(f"Deleted batch of {batch_deleted} nodes")

                # Clear Source nodes
                session.run("MATCH (s:Source) DETACH DELETE s", timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT).consume()

            logger.info(f"Cleared {progress.nodes} nodes and {progress.relationships} relationships")
            record_destructive_op("clear_all", target="neo4j", affected=progress.nodes, scope="every node")
            return True

        except Exception as e:
            # A delete that fails part-way is recorded with what it deleted, before a retry or the
            # False return.
            self._record_failed_clear("clear_all", "every node", progress, e)
            if isinstance(e, _CLEAR_RETRYABLE_ERRORS):
                raise  # let @retry_with_backoff handle transient errors
            logger.error(f"Error clearing Neo4j: {e}")
            return False

    @staticmethod
    def _count_clear_scope(session: Any, node: str) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Counts of the edgeguard-only clear for the node pattern ``node`` (``_clear_scope_pattern``):
        ``managed`` — the nodes it deletes (``edgeguard_managed = true``); ``others`` — the nodes it
        keeps; ``enriched`` — the kept nodes EdgeGuard wrote to (``edgeguard_enriched = true``)."""
        managed = session.run(
            f"MATCH {node} WHERE n.edgeguard_managed = true RETURN count(n) AS count",
            timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
        ).single()["count"]
        others = session.run(
            f"MATCH {node} WHERE coalesce(n.edgeguard_managed, false) <> true RETURN count(n) AS count",
            timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
        ).single()["count"]
        enriched = session.run(
            f"MATCH {node} WHERE coalesce(n.edgeguard_managed, false) <> true AND n.edgeguard_enriched = true "
            "RETURN count(n) AS count",
            timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
        ).single()["count"]
        return {"managed": managed, "others": others, "enriched": enriched}

    def count_edgeguard_managed(self, label: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """What ``clear_edgeguard_managed(label)`` would delete and keep, without deleting (2026-10).

        Returns ``{"managed", "others", "enriched"}`` (see ``_count_clear_scope``); ``managed +
        others`` is every node in the scope's label, or in the database without a label. Used by
        ``scripts/clear_neo4j.py`` for its preview. Raises ValueError for a label outside the
        allow-list (before any statement) and the driver's error when Neo4j cannot answer.
        """
        node = _clear_scope_pattern(label)
        if not self.driver:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot count: no connection to Neo4j")
        with self.driver.session() as session:
            return self._count_clear_scope(session, node)

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def clear_edgeguard_managed(self, label: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
        """Delete only the nodes EdgeGuard created (2026-10, fresh-baseline PR).

        Scoped by the ownership marker ``n.edgeguard_managed = true``, which every
        node MERGE stamps on its create path only. Nodes EdgeGuard merely wrote to
        (``edgeguard_enriched = true`` — a partner created them first) and nodes it
        never touched — ResilMesh's topology, identity and mission layers on a shared
        database — are left in place, EdgeGuard's properties on them included.
        ``DETACH DELETE`` also removes every relationship attached to a deleted node,
        including any a partner drew to it; that is unavoidable when the node goes.
        ``label`` narrows the delete, and the counts, to that one label
        (``scripts/clear_neo4j.py --label``); a label outside the allow-list raises
        ValueError before any statement runs.

        Returns:
            True if successful, False otherwise
        """
        node = _clear_scope_pattern(label)
        what = "EdgeGuard-managed nodes" if label is None else f"EdgeGuard-managed {label} nodes"
        scope = "edgeguard_managed = true" if label is None else f"edgeguard_managed = true AND n:{label}"
        if not self.driver:
            logger.error("Cannot clear: no connection to Neo4j")
            return False

        progress = _ClearProgress()
        details: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        try:
            logger.warning("Clearing %s (edgeguard_managed = true) from Neo4j...", what)
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                counts = self._count_clear_scope(session, node)
                node_count, others, enriched = counts["managed"], counts["others"], counts["enriched"]
                logger.info(
                    "EdgeGuard-created nodes: %s; nodes left untouched: %s (of which EdgeGuard-enriched: %s)",
                    node_count,
                    others,
                    enriched,
                )
                details = {"left_untouched": others, "enriched_kept": enriched}
                if label is not None:
                    details["label"] = label

                # Relationships touching a marked node first, in bounded batches (same heap
                # reason as clear_all); a relationship on a node that goes, goes with it.
                self._delete_relationships_batched(
                    session, f"MATCH {node}-[r]-() WHERE n.edgeguard_managed = true", progress=progress
                )

                while progress.nodes < node_count:
                    result = session.run(
                        f"MATCH {node} WHERE n.edgeguard_managed = true WITH n LIMIT {self._CLEAR_NODE_BATCH} "
                        "DETACH DELETE n RETURN count(n) AS deleted",
                        timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
                    )
                    batch_deleted = result.single()["deleted"]
                    if batch_deleted == 0:
                        break
                    progress.nodes += batch_deleted
                    logger.debug(f"Deleted batch of {batch_deleted} EdgeGuard-managed nodes")

            logger.info(f"Cleared {progress.nodes} {what} and {progress.relationships} relationships")
            record_destructive_op(
                "clear_edgeguard_managed",
                target="neo4j",
                affected=progress.nodes,
                scope=scope,
                details=details,
            )
            return True

        except Exception as e:
            # Recorded with what this attempt deleted, before a retry or the False return.
            self._record_failed_clear("clear_edgeguard_managed", scope, progress, e, details)
            if isinstance(e, _CLEAR_RETRYABLE_ERRORS):
                raise  # let @retry_with_backoff handle transient errors
            logger.error(f"Error clearing EdgeGuard-managed data from Neo4j: {e}")
            return False

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def create_constraints(self) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """
        Create UNIQUE constraints with error handling.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (success_count, error_count)
        """
        if not self.driver:
            logger.error("Cannot create constraints: no connection")
            return 0, 0

        # Migration: drop old compound (name/cve_id, tag) constraints before creating
        # single-key ones. Harmless if they don't exist (IF EXISTS).
        old_constraints = [
            "DROP CONSTRAINT cve_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT vulnerability_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT malware_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT actor_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT technique_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT tactic_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT campaign_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT tool_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT indicator_key IF EXISTS",
            # Drop old compound CVSS constraints (cve_id, tag) → single-key (cve_id)
            "DROP CONSTRAINT cvssv31_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT cvssv2_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT cvssv30_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT cvssv40_key IF EXISTS",
            # 2026-10 shared-database contract: UNIQUE constraints EdgeGuard used to declare on
            # partner-owned labels (SHARED_LABELS_WITHOUT_UNIQUE_CONSTRAINT). Dropped on every run
            # so a database created by an older build converges without manual DDL; a no-op once absent.
            "DROP CONSTRAINT device_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT networkservice_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT softwareversion_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT application_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT role_key IF EXISTS",
            "DROP CONSTRAINT user_key IF EXISTS",
        ]
        with self.driver.session() as session:
            for stmt in old_constraints:
                try:
                    session.run(stmt, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT).consume()
                except Exception as drop_err:
                    # PR #33 round 13: silent ``except: pass`` replaced with a
                    # DEBUG log so an operator running in verbose mode can see
                    # which old-constraint drops were no-ops vs which silently
                    # masked a real schema error. Most invocations are no-ops
                    # (constraint already absent on a fresh DB), so DEBUG is
                    # the right level — INFO would spam.
                    logger.debug("Drop legacy constraint %r: %s (likely already absent)", stmt[:60], drop_err)

            # Deduplicate CVSS nodes before creating single-key constraints.
            # Old compound key (cve_id, tag) may have created multiple nodes per CVE.
            # Keep the first node (by elementId), move relationships, delete duplicates.
            for cvss_label in ("CVSSv31", "CVSSv30", "CVSSv2", "CVSSv40"):
                try:
                    dedup_result = session.run(
                        f"""
                        MATCH (n:{cvss_label})
                        // 2026-10: never group on a null key (every key-less node would fall into one
                        // group and all but the first be deleted) and never touch partner-created nodes.
                        WHERE n.cve_id IS NOT NULL AND n.edgeguard_managed = true
                        WITH n.cve_id AS cid, collect(n) AS nodes
                        WHERE size(nodes) > 1
                        WITH nodes[0] AS keep, nodes[1..] AS dups
                        UNWIND dups AS dup
                        // The keeper already carries the CVE edge; the duplicate's relationships go with it.
                        WITH keep, dup
                        OPTIONAL MATCH (dup)-[r]-()
                        DELETE r
                        DETACH DELETE dup
                        RETURN count(dup) AS removed
                        """,
                        timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
                    )
                    row = dedup_result.single()
                    removed = row["removed"] if row else 0
                    if removed > 0:
                        logger.info("CVSS dedup: removed %s duplicate %s nodes", removed, cvss_label)
                        record_destructive_op("cvss_dedup", target="neo4j", affected=removed, scope=cvss_label)
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.debug("CVSS dedup for %s skipped: %s", cvss_label, e)

        constraints = [
            # Source nodes
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT source_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (s:Source) REQUIRE (s.source_id) IS UNIQUE",
            # CVE / Vulnerability — separate labels kept for backward compat
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT cve_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (c:CVE) REQUIRE (c.cve_id) IS UNIQUE",
            # Vulnerability: match the 2-field MERGE key used in merge_vulnerabilities_batch
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT vulnerability_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (v:Vulnerability) REQUIRE (v.cve_id) IS UNIQUE",
            # Indicator: match the 2-field MERGE key used in merge_indicators_batch
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT indicator_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (i:Indicator) REQUIRE (i.indicator_type, i.value) IS UNIQUE",
            # Threat-graph node types
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT malware_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (m:Malware) REQUIRE (m.name) IS UNIQUE",
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT actor_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (a:ThreatActor) REQUIRE (a.name) IS UNIQUE",
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT technique_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (t:Technique) REQUIRE (t.mitre_id) IS UNIQUE",
            # MITRE tactics — 14 fixed nodes; unique by mitre_id only
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT tactic_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (t:Tactic) REQUIRE (t.mitre_id) IS UNIQUE",
            # Tool nodes — MITRE tools, keyed by mitre_id only
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT tool_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (t:Tool) REQUIRE (t.mitre_id) IS UNIQUE",
            # Sector nodes — created dynamically; must stay unique by name
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT sector_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (s:Sector) REQUIRE (s.name) IS UNIQUE",
            # CVSS sub-nodes — one per CVE (CVSS scores are properties of the vuln, not the source)
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT cvssv31_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:CVSSv31) REQUIRE (n.cve_id) IS UNIQUE",
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT cvssv2_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:CVSSv2) REQUIRE (n.cve_id) IS UNIQUE",
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT cvssv30_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:CVSSv30) REQUIRE (n.cve_id) IS UNIQUE",
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT cvssv40_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:CVSSv40) REQUIRE (n.cve_id) IS UNIQUE",
            # Campaign nodes — one per actor, keyed by name only
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT campaign_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (c:Campaign) REQUIRE (c.name) IS UNIQUE",
            # PR #34 round 26 (invariant audit): added the missing 10 UNIQUE
            # constraints to match the labels declared in
            # ``node_identity._NATURAL_KEYS``. Without these, two concurrent
            # MERGEs on the same logical (label, key) could create duplicate
            # nodes — silently violating the deterministic-uuid contract that
            # underpins delta sync. Pinned by
            # ``test_every_natural_key_label_has_a_unique_constraint``.
            # ResilMesh / topology — only the keys that are unique in CRUSOE's own model as well.
            # 2026-10: Device / NetworkService / SoftwareVersion / Application / Role / User are no
            # longer constrained (SHARED_LABELS_WITHOUT_UNIQUE_CONSTRAINT): their keys recur
            # legitimately in the partner's data, so a UNIQUE created here made the partner's own
            # writes fail. Instances an older build created are dropped above.
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT ip_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:IP) REQUIRE (n.address) IS UNIQUE",
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT host_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Host) REQUIRE (n.hostname) IS UNIQUE",
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT subnet_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Subnet) REQUIRE (n.range) IS UNIQUE",
            # Alert: alert_id is the upstream-provided idempotency key.
            "CREATE CONSTRAINT alert_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Alert) REQUIRE (n.alert_id) IS UNIQUE",
        ]

        success_count = 0
        error_count = 0

        with self.driver.session() as session:
            for constraint in constraints:
                try:
                    session.run(constraint, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT).consume()
                    logger.info(f"Constraint created: {constraint[:50]}...")
                    success_count += 1
                except neo4j_exceptions.DatabaseError as e:
                    # Constraint may already exist or be unsupported
                    logger.debug(f"Constraint (may exist): {e}")
                    success_count += 1  # Not a failure if it exists
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.warning(f"Constraint error: {e}")
                    error_count += 1

        logger.info(f"Constraints: {success_count} succeeded, {error_count} failed")
        return success_count, error_count

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def ensure_sources(self) -> bool:
        """
        Ensure one Source node per registered source, keyed by its canonical id (``SOURCES``), and
        delete an EdgeGuard Source node keyed by a registry alias that has no relationship.

        Returns:
            True if successful
        """
        if not self.driver:
            logger.error("Cannot ensure sources: no connection")
            return False

        try:
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                for source_id, info in SOURCES.items():
                    # Deterministic Source uuid — referenced by SOURCED_FROM edges'
                    # trg_uuid stamping in merge_indicators_batch / merge_vulnerabilities_batch.
                    source_uuid = compute_node_uuid("Source", {"source_id": source_id})
                    query = """
                    MERGE (s:Source {source_id: $source_id})
                    ON CREATE SET s.created_at = datetime(),
                                  s.uuid = $source_uuid,
                                  s.edgeguard_managed = true
                    ON MATCH SET s.edgeguard_enriched = CASE WHEN s.edgeguard_managed = true THEN s.edgeguard_enriched ELSE true END
                    SET s.name = $name,
                        s.type = $type,
                        s.reliability = $reliability,
                        s.updated_at = datetime(),
                        s.uuid = coalesce(s.uuid, $source_uuid)
                    """
                    session.run(
                        query,
                        source_id=source_id,
                        source_uuid=source_uuid,
                        name=info["name"],
                        type=info["type"],
                        reliability=info["reliability"],
                        timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
                    ).consume()

                # A Source node keyed by a registry alias (``otx``, ``cisa``, ...) is never created; one
                # that a graph still holds and that has no relationship is deleted. Only EdgeGuard's own
                # nodes (``edgeguard_managed``) qualify; one with a relationship is kept.
                canonical_ids = {src.canonical_id for src in source_registry.all_sources()}
                alias_ids = sorted(source_registry.all_aliases() - canonical_ids)
                record = session.run(
                    """
                    MATCH (stale:Source)
                    WHERE stale.source_id IN $alias_ids AND stale.edgeguard_managed = true AND NOT EXISTS { (stale)--() }
                    WITH stale, stale.source_id AS source_id
                    DELETE stale
                    RETURN count(source_id) AS deleted, collect(source_id) AS source_ids
                    """,
                    alias_ids=alias_ids,
                    timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
                ).single()
                deleted = record["deleted"] if record else 0
                if isinstance(deleted, int) and deleted > 0:
                    deleted_ids = sorted(str(sid) for sid in (record["source_ids"] or []))
                    logger.info(
                        f"Deleted {deleted} Source node(s) keyed by a registry alias with no relationship: "
                        + ", ".join(deleted_ids)
                    )
                    record_destructive_op(
                        "source_alias_cleanup",
                        target="neo4j",
                        affected=deleted,
                        scope="Source keyed by a registry alias, edgeguard_managed, no relationship",
                        details={"source_ids": deleted_ids},
                    )

            logger.info(f"Ensured {len(SOURCES)} Source nodes exist")
            return True

        except (
            neo4j_exceptions.ServiceUnavailable,
            neo4j_exceptions.TransientError,
            ConnectionError,
            TimeoutError,
        ):
            raise  # let @retry_with_backoff handle transient errors
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error ensuring sources: {e}")
            return False

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def apply_sector_labels(self) -> int:
        """
        Apply secondary sector labels (e.g. :Finance, :Healthcare) to all nodes that
        carry a non-'global' zone value.  Labels are derived from the node's ``zone``
        list property and are applied with APOC so the label name is dynamic.

        This must be called *after* nodes have been merged so that the ``zone``
        property is already present.

        Returns:
            Number of nodes that received at least one new sector label.
        """
        if not self.driver:
            logger.error("Cannot apply sector labels: no connection")
            return 0

        # Scope to EdgeGuard-managed node labels only — avoids a full-graph scan
        # (`MATCH (n)`) and prevents accidentally labelling nodes from other
        # applications that share the same Neo4j instance.
        edgeguard_labels = [
            "Indicator",
            "Vulnerability",
            "Malware",
            "ThreatActor",
            "Technique",
            "Tactic",
            "Campaign",
            "Tool",
            "Source",
            "CVE",
        ]
        per_label_query = """
        MATCH (n:{label})
        WHERE n.zone IS NOT NULL AND size(n.zone) > 0
        WITH n, [z IN n.zone WHERE z <> 'global' | apoc.text.capitalize(z)] AS sectorLabels
        WHERE size(sectorLabels) > 0
        CALL apoc.create.addLabels(n, sectorLabels) YIELD node
        RETURN count(DISTINCT node) AS labeled
        """

        total_labeled = 0
        try:
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                for lbl in edgeguard_labels:
                    _validate_label(lbl)
                    result = session.run(per_label_query.format(label=lbl), timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT)
                    record = result.single()
                    total_labeled += record["labeled"] if record else 0
            logger.info(f"Applied sector labels to {total_labeled} nodes")
            return total_labeled
        except (
            neo4j_exceptions.ServiceUnavailable,
            neo4j_exceptions.TransientError,
            ConnectionError,
            TimeoutError,
        ):
            raise  # let @retry_with_backoff handle transient errors
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error applying sector labels: {e}")
            return 0

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def merge_node_with_source(
        self,
        label: str,
        key_props: Dict,
        data: Dict,
        source_id: str,
        extra_props: Dict = None,
        fill_props: Optional[Dict] = None,
        description: Optional[RankedDescription] = None,
        refresh_raw_data: bool = False,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Merge a node with proper source tracking.

        PR-N16 Fix #3 (HIGH, 2026-04-22 pre-baseline merge-audit):
        decorated with ``@retry_with_backoff`` so single-item merge
        paths (``merge_indicator``, ``merge_malware``, ``merge_actor``,
        ``merge_technique``, ``merge_tactic``, ``merge_tool``,
        ``merge_cve``, ``merge_vulnerability``, topology mergers) retry
        on Neo4j transient errors (deadlock, lock timeout, GC pause,
        cluster failover) — not just the batched paths that PR-N15
        hardened. At 730-day baseline scale, single-item merges of
        Malware/Actor/MITRE nodes are foundational — a transient that
        drops one Malware node silently breaks every downstream
        `create_misp_relationships_batch` INDICATES edge referencing it.

        Args:
            label: Node label (e.g., 'Indicator', 'Vulnerability')
            key_props: Dict of key properties for MERGE
            data: Dict of all properties to store
            source_id: The source providing this data
            extra_props: Additional properties to set on the node (beyond standard fields)
            fill_props: Properties set only where the node has no value (2026-10,
                ``_set_if_absent_clause``); a key also in ``extra_props`` is set from there
            description: The record's description with its source and that source's rank
                (2026-10-16): set with ``description_source`` when the source ranks at least as
                high as the stored description's (``description_ranking``). A label with a
                description ranking takes ``description`` and ``description_source`` only from
                here, never from ``extra_props`` or ``fill_props``.
            refresh_raw_data: Replace ``SOURCED_FROM.raw_data`` with this record on every write
                (2026-10, ``merge_cve``), so the edge holds the source's latest record; otherwise it is
                written when the edge is created only.

        Returns:
            True if successful
        """
        if not self.driver:
            logger.error("Cannot merge node: no connection")
            return False
        # The canonical id, as in the batch writers: the node's ``source`` default, ``last_imported_from``
        # and report source name the ``Source`` node its ``SOURCED_FROM`` edge reaches (``SOURCES`` above).
        source_id = source_registry.canonical_source_id(source_id) or source_id

        # 2026-10-16: refused before the statement is built, so a caller that bypasses the ranking fails
        # loudly instead of being logged as a terminal write error.
        ranking = ranking_for_label(label)
        bypass = _RANKED_DESCRIPTION_PROPS & (set(extra_props or {}) | set(fill_props or {}))
        if ranking is not None and bypass:
            raise ValueError(f"merge_node_with_source: {label} {sorted(bypass)} are written through the source ranking")
        if description is not None and ranking is None:
            raise ValueError(f"merge_node_with_source: {label} has no description ranking")

        try:
            # Validate property names before interpolating into Cypher.
            for k in key_props:
                _validate_prop_name(k)
            # Build key property assignments
            key_set = ", ".join([f"{k}: ${k}" for k in key_props.keys()])

            # Serialize raw data to JSON string for storage
            raw_data = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k not in key_props}

            # Get source as array (like zone)
            source_array = _canonical_source_list(data.get("source", [source_id]))

            # Include original_source if present in the data
            original_source = data.get("original_source")
            if original_source:
                raw_data["original_source"] = original_source

            raw_data_json = json.dumps(raw_data, default=str)

            # PR-N14 Fix #2 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit): clamp
            # confidence_score to [0.0, 1.0] + reject non-finite (inf/
            # nan). A compromised feed shipping ``confidence_score:
            # "1e309"`` would otherwise pin ``r.confidence_score = inf``
            # on every max-wins upsert. Fall back to 0.5 on bad input
            # (same default as the missing-field case).
            _claimed_conf = data.get("confidence_score")
            _clamped_conf = clamp_confidence_score(_claimed_conf)
            if _claimed_conf is not None and _clamped_conf is None:
                logger.warning(
                    "confidence_score rejected by clamp for %s/%s (claimed=%r) — "
                    "falling back to 0.5. Compromised feed?",
                    label,
                    source_id,
                    _claimed_conf,
                )
            confidence = _clamped_conf if _clamped_conf is not None else 0.5
            zone = data.get("zone", ["global"])  # zone is an array
            # Accumulate tag into tags array (tag removed from MERGE key)
            tag_value = data.get("tag", source_id)
            tag_array = [tag_value] if tag_value else [source_id]

            _validate_label(label)

            # Deterministic per-node UUID — uuid5(namespace, canonical(label, key_props)).
            # Stable across machines and Neo4j instances so the cloud copy of a
            # local Indicator has the same n.uuid; edges carry src_uuid/trg_uuid
            # that resolve correctly cross-environment. Computed here from the
            # actual MERGE key (not the label's documented natural key) so the
            # uuid always matches what the Cypher MERGE binds to.
            node_uuid = compute_node_uuid(label, key_props)

            # PR #34 round 24: apply "specifics-override-global" at accumulation
            # time — see _zone_override_global_clause for full rationale.
            _zone_clause = _zone_override_global_clause("n", "$zone")
            # PR (S5) (architecture redesign): source-truthful
            # timestamps moved OFF the node and ONTO the per-source
            # SOURCED_FROM edge. The node now carries only DB-local
            # facts (first_imported_at / last_updated) which cannot be
            # misread as "first observed in reality" claims. The
            # extractor's output is still pulled from data here and
            # threaded through to ``_upsert_sourced_relationship``
            # below, where it lives on the (n)-[r:SOURCED_FROM]->(s)
            # edge as ``r.source_reported_first_at`` /
            # ``r.source_reported_last_at`` with MIN/MAX CASE semantics.
            first_seen_at_source = data.get("first_seen_at_source")
            last_seen_at_source = data.get("last_seen_at_source")
            # 2026-10-16 (indicator aging): an Indicator keeps the highest confidence a source gave
            # (``source_confidence``), records the report the data carries (MISP sync items carry
            # one; the STIX import and the VirusTotal re-enrichment do not, so they never advance
            # the basis) and gets its ``confidence_score`` and lifecycle from the one rule. Any
            # other label keeps the max-wins confidence and gets ``active`` on create only.
            is_indicator = label == "Indicator"
            if is_indicator:
                confidence_items = f"""{source_confidence_item("n", "$confidence")},
                {node_report_items("n", "$report", "$source_id")},"""
                create_items = ""
            else:
                confidence_items = """n.confidence_score = CASE
                    WHEN n.confidence_score IS NULL OR $confidence > n.confidence_score
                    THEN $confidence
                    ELSE n.confidence_score END,"""
                create_items = f",\n                          {_create_active('n')}"
            query = f"""
            MERGE (n:{label} {{{key_set}}})
            ON CREATE SET n.first_imported_at = datetime(),
                          n.uuid = $node_uuid,
                          n.edgeguard_managed = true{create_items}
            ON MATCH SET n.edgeguard_enriched = CASE WHEN n.edgeguard_managed = true THEN n.edgeguard_enriched ELSE true END

            // Always accumulate sources and zones — provenance is never overwritten.
            // Use APOC to deduplicate the merged arrays in one step.
            SET {confidence_items}
                n.source = {_dedup_concat_clause("n.source", "$source_array")},
                {_zone_clause},
                n.tags = {_dedup_concat_clause("n.tags", "$tag_array")},
                n.tag = coalesce(n.tag, $tag_value),
                n.last_updated = datetime(),
                n.last_imported_from = $source_id,
                // n.uuid is deterministic — coalesce so we never overwrite it.
                // (Defensive only; same input always produces same uuid, but if a
                // node was created before this code was deployed it will get the
                // uuid stamped here on next MERGE.)
                n.uuid = coalesce(n.uuid, $node_uuid)"""

            # PR #33 round 10: dropped legacy scalars misp_event_id / misp_attribute_id
            # (pre-release, no real data to migrate). Multi-event provenance lives only
            # in the misp_event_ids[] / misp_attribute_ids[] arrays, accumulated
            # via apoc.coll.toSet so duplicates within an array are de-duped.
            misp_event_id = data.get("misp_event_id")
            if misp_event_id:
                query += f""",
                n.misp_event_ids = {_dedup_concat_clause("n.misp_event_ids", "[$misp_event_id]")}"""

            misp_attribute_id = data.get("misp_attribute_id")
            if misp_attribute_id:
                query += f""",
                n.misp_attribute_ids = {_dedup_concat_clause("n.misp_attribute_ids", "[$misp_attribute_id]")}"""

            # PR #34 round 17: deleted ``n.original_published_date`` and
            # ``n.original_modified_date`` SET clauses. They were intended to
            # capture the upstream NVD ``published`` / ``last_modified`` dates,
            # but every non-NVD path (CISA KEV, OTX, MISP-event-only) silently
            # fell back to the MISP event date — making the field name lie
            # ("original" really means "first-seen-by-EdgeGuard"). The
            # canonical EdgeGuard first-touch / last-modified values already
            # live in ``first_imported_at`` (precise timestamp + TZ) and
            # ``last_updated``. Zero readers in production: no GraphQL field,
            # no STIX export, no Cypher consumer, no doc reference.

            # PR #34 round 18: deleted ``n.original_source`` SET clause +
            # the matching index. The Neo4j property had ZERO production
            # readers (no GraphQL field, no STIX export, no Cypher
            # MATCH/WHERE). The Python helper that EXTRACTS original_source
            # from MISP tags is alive (line 847 above) — it's stored on the
            # SOURCED_FROM edge's r.raw_data JSON for audit trail, and the
            # extraction in misp_collector derives the canonical `source`
            # field. Only the dead n.original_source write is removed.

            # Add extra_props (aliases, description, etc.) if provided.
            # Validate every property name before interpolating into Cypher.
            # Array properties that should ACCUMULATE (deduplicated) across sources,
            # not overwrite. Scalar properties are set with last-write-wins.
            # 2026-10 audit: the 50 cap was sized for aliases (p99 ≈ 30) but was applied to every
            # accumulating list — MITRE groups carry up to 130 `uses_techniques` (27/172 exceed 50) and
            # the writer sends up to 400 (`_technique_meta`), so the node kept the first 50 and ~670
            # `mitre_explicit` edges could never exist. Technique / software / report lists get their
            # own ceilings (≥ the writer's caps); `aliases` and the rest keep 50.
            _ARRAY_ITEM_CAPS = {
                "uses_techniques": 512,
                "reported_techniques": 512,
                "pulse_ids": 512,
                "uses_malware": 256,
                "uses_tools": 256,
            }
            _ARRAY_ACCUMULATE_PROPS = frozenset(
                {
                    "aliases",
                    "malware_types",
                    "uses_techniques",
                    "tactic_phases",
                    # 2026-10: pulse-level technique ids and source-report ids
                    # accumulate across pulses like the other list props.
                    "reported_techniques",
                    "pulse_ids",
                    "uses_malware",
                    "uses_tools",
                }
            )
            # PR-N14 Fix #3 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit): cardinality
            # cap + placeholder-entry filter for accumulating array
            # properties. A compromised feed can otherwise ship
            # ``aliases=["a1",...,"a100000"]`` and grow a Malware
            # node's aliases to 10M entries over several syncs —
            # the Q2 alias-match then walks that array per-row,
            # OOM-crashing the relationship build. Also drop placeholder-name entries
            # (``"unknown"``, ``"n/a"``, …) to mirror the PR-N10
            # reject of placeholder node NAMES to their aliases lists.
            #
            # 50 is generous — MITRE / Malpedia malware corpora have
            # p99 ≈ 30 aliases per family. Truncation policy: keep
            # the FIRST 50 non-placeholder entries (stable order),
            # log-and-drop the rest.
            _MAX_ARRAY_ITEMS = 50
            _MAX_ARRAY_ITEM_LEN = 200  # chars per individual entry

            def _sanitize_array_value(prop: str, items: list) -> list:
                """Drop placeholder entries, truncate overlong strings,
                cap cardinality. Returns a new list (does NOT mutate)."""
                out: list = []
                dropped_placeholder = 0
                for entry in items:
                    if not isinstance(entry, str):
                        # Non-strings pass through (e.g. numeric
                        # malware_types in some feeds); only placeholder
                        # name fields are filtered.
                        out.append(entry)
                        continue
                    stripped = entry.strip()
                    if not stripped:
                        continue
                    # Filter placeholder-name entries from accumulating
                    # arrays. Uses the same canonical set as PR-N10's
                    # merge-key reject.
                    if prop == "aliases" and is_placeholder_name(stripped):
                        dropped_placeholder += 1
                        continue
                    if len(stripped) > _MAX_ARRAY_ITEM_LEN:
                        stripped = stripped[:_MAX_ARRAY_ITEM_LEN]
                    out.append(stripped)
                if dropped_placeholder:
                    logger.info(
                        "PR-N14: dropped %d placeholder entries from %s[%s] during merge "
                        "(e.g. 'unknown'/'apt'/'n/a' — would otherwise create false-hub "
                        "alias matches in Q2/Q9)",
                        dropped_placeholder,
                        label,
                        prop,
                    )
                cap = _ARRAY_ITEM_CAPS.get(prop, _MAX_ARRAY_ITEMS)
                if len(out) > cap:
                    logger.warning(
                        "PR-N14: %s[%s] incoming size %d exceeds cap %d — truncating to "
                        "first %d entries (stable order). A compromised feed may be "
                        "shipping an unbounded alias list.",
                        label,
                        prop,
                        len(out),
                        cap,
                        cap,
                    )
                    out = out[:cap]
                return out

            extra_props = dict(extra_props or {})
            # 2026-10 (fresh-baseline PR): TLP travels as a ``tlp:<level>`` MISP tag,
            # is rehydrated into ``item["tlp"]`` by the sync, and lands on every
            # node that goes through this chokepoint (CVE, Malware, ThreatActor,
            # Technique, Tactic, Tool). Indicators use the batch path, which
            # promotes it explicitly.
            if data.get("tlp") and "tlp" not in extra_props:
                extra_props["tlp"] = str(data["tlp"])
            params_extra = {}
            for prop_name, prop_value in extra_props.items():
                _validate_prop_name(prop_name)
                if prop_value is not None and prop_value != "":
                    # PR-N16 Fix #1 (BLOCK, 2026-04-22 pre-baseline merge-audit):
                    # for accumulating-array props, ALWAYS take the list
                    # accumulation path — coerce scalars to a single-
                    # element list if the caller passed a string.
                    # Pre-PR-N16 the ``isinstance(prop_value, list)``
                    # check silently fell through to the scalar SET
                    # branch (``SET n.aliases = $aliases``), which
                    # OVERWROTE the accumulated list with a scalar
                    # string — destroying every alias from previous
                    # syncs. MISP objects emit string-typed
                    # ``aliases`` / ``malware_types`` attributes
                    # commonly (misp_collector.py:385,410,478,498);
                    # this bug fired on every overlap and broke
                    # downstream alias-based relationship MATCHes
                    # (Q2/Q9 + create_malware_actor_relationship).
                    if prop_name in _ARRAY_ACCUMULATE_PROPS:
                        if isinstance(prop_value, (list, tuple)):
                            prop_value = list(prop_value)
                        elif isinstance(prop_value, str):
                            # Scalar string → single-element list.
                            # Strip whitespace; empty-after-strip →
                            # skip (same semantic as the outer
                            # ``!= ""`` gate).
                            stripped = prop_value.strip()
                            if not stripped:
                                continue
                            prop_value = [stripped]
                        else:
                            # Non-list / non-string (int, dict, …) —
                            # cannot safely merge into an array. Log
                            # + skip rather than corrupt.
                            logger.warning(
                                "PR-N16: %s[%s] skipped — incoming value type %s "
                                "is neither list nor string; cannot merge into "
                                "accumulating-array property. value=%r",
                                label,
                                prop_name,
                                type(prop_value).__name__,
                                prop_value,
                            )
                            continue
                        prop_value = _sanitize_array_value(prop_name, prop_value)
                        if not prop_value:
                            # Sanitization left an empty list — skip
                            # emitting the SET clause entirely.
                            continue
                        query += f", n.{prop_name} = {_dedup_concat_clause(f'n.{prop_name}', f'${prop_name}')}"
                    elif prop_name == "tlp":
                        query += f", n.tlp = {_tlp_most_restrictive_clause('n.tlp', '$tlp')}"
                    else:
                        query += f", n.{prop_name} = ${prop_name}"
                    params_extra[prop_name] = prop_value

            # 2026-10: values a record may supply but must not replace (a CVE's dates from any record but
            # NVD's, ``merge_cve``) are set only where the node has none. The parameter is prefixed so it
            # cannot collide with a standard parameter of this statement.
            for prop_name, prop_value in (fill_props or {}).items():
                _validate_prop_name(prop_name)
                if prop_name in extra_props or prop_value is None or prop_value == "":
                    continue
                query += f", n.{prop_name} = {_set_if_absent_clause(f'n.{prop_name}', f'$fill_{prop_name}')}"
                params_extra[f"fill_{prop_name}"] = prop_value

            # 2026-10-16: an Indicator's aging, in a SET clause of its own after the one above: the rule
            # reads the report and ``source_confidence`` that clause recorded (``indicator_aging``).
            if is_indicator:
                query += "\n            " + aging_set_clause("n")

            # 2026-10-16: the description and its source, by the source ranking of the label
            # (``description_ranking``), decided once after every other property is set.
            if description is not None and ranking is not None:
                query += "\n" + ranking.set_cypher(
                    "n", "n", "$ranked_description", "$ranked_description_source", "$ranked_description_rank"
                )
                params_extra["ranked_description"] = description.text
                params_extra["ranked_description_source"] = description.source
                params_extra["ranked_description_rank"] = description.rank

            if params_extra:
                key_str = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in key_props.items())
                logger.debug(
                    "MERGE %s(%s): promoting %s to node properties",
                    label,
                    key_str,
                    list(params_extra.keys()),
                )

            # Check existing confidence before update for audit logging. 2026-10-16: an Indicator's
            # comparison value is the confidence a source gave (``source_confidence``; a node written
            # before has only ``confidence_score``), not its aged ``confidence_score``.
            confidence_expr = (
                "coalesce(n.source_confidence, n.confidence_score)" if is_indicator else "n.confidence_score"
            )
            check_query = f"""
            MATCH (n:{label} {{{key_set}}})
            RETURN {confidence_expr} as existing_confidence, n.source as existing_source,
                   n.retired_at as retired_at, n.retired_by as retired_by
            """

            with self.driver.session() as session:
                # Check existing values for audit
                existing = session.run(check_query, **{k: v for k, v in key_props.items()}, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT)
                existing_record = existing.single()

                if existing_record:
                    existing_conf = existing_record.get("existing_confidence")
                    existing_src = existing_record.get("existing_source")
                    key_str = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in key_props.items())
                    if existing_conf is not None and confidence < existing_conf:
                        logger.info(
                            f"AUDIT: Keeping the higher confidence of {label}({key_str}): "
                            f"existing={existing_conf} (source={existing_src}), new={confidence} (source={source_id})"
                        )
                    # 2026-10-16: a retired node written again. A manual decommission stays; an
                    # Indicator's decay retirement is recomputed from its report time by the aging rule.
                    existing_retired = existing_record.get("retired_at")
                    if existing_retired is not None:
                        logger.info(
                            "AUDIT: Re-imported retired node %s(%s): retired_by=%s, retired_at=%s, source=%s — %s",
                            label,
                            key_str,
                            existing_record.get("retired_by"),
                            existing_retired,
                            source_id,
                            "the aging rule decides from the report time"
                            if is_indicator and existing_record.get("retired_by") == "decay"
                            else "kept",
                        )

                # Execute the merge
                params = {
                    **key_props,
                    "source_id": source_id,
                    "source_array": source_array,
                    "confidence": confidence,
                    "zone": zone,
                    "tag_array": tag_array,
                    "tag_value": tag_value,
                    "node_uuid": node_uuid,
                    **params_extra,
                }
                if is_indicator:
                    # 2026-10-16: the report the data carries (all None without one).
                    params["report"] = report_row(data)
                # PR (S5) (architecture redesign + bugbot 9e58af6 LOW):
                # source-truthful timestamps live on the SOURCED_FROM
                # edge (not the node), so they are NOT bound into the
                # node MERGE params dict above. They are passed
                # separately to ``_upsert_sourced_relationship`` below
                # via the ``source_reported_first_at`` /
                # ``source_reported_last_at`` keyword arguments.
                # The local ``first_seen_at_source`` / ``last_seen_at_source``
                # variables read from ``data`` are used for that pass-
                # through ONLY.
                if misp_event_id:
                    params["misp_event_id"] = misp_event_id
                if misp_attribute_id:
                    params["misp_attribute_id"] = misp_attribute_id
                if original_source:
                    params["original_source"] = original_source
                # PR #34 round 17 historical context: removed the lossy
                # ``first_seen`` / ``last_seen_val`` params along with the
                # NVD-specific ``original_published_date``/``original_modified_date``
                # SET clauses. PR (S5) reintroduces SOURCE-TRUTHFUL
                # timestamps as separate, allowlist-gated fields
                # (``first_seen_at_source`` / ``last_seen_at_source``)
                # bound above, so the previous semantic-conflation bug
                # doesn't return.
                # 2026-10-16: read the result inside this try: an error the server meets while
                # executing or committing the MERGE arrives with it, and only here does it reach the
                # retry (``_is_retryable_neo4j_error``) or the ``return False`` below.
                session.run(query, **params, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT).consume()

            # Now create/update the SOURCED_FROM relationship with raw data
            # PR (S5): per-source timestamps now live on the
            # edge (not the node). Thread the source-truthful values
            # through so the edge MERGE can MIN/MAX them per source.
            return self._upsert_sourced_relationship(
                label,
                key_props,
                source_id,
                raw_data_json,
                confidence,
                source_reported_first_at=first_seen_at_source,
                source_reported_last_at=last_seen_at_source,
                misp_event_id=misp_event_id,
                source_refs=data.get("source_refs"),
                report=report_row(data) if is_indicator else None,
                zones=zone,
                stated_zones=data.get("stated_zones"),
                stated_refs=data.get("stated_refs"),
                refresh_raw_data=refresh_raw_data,
            )

        except (
            neo4j_exceptions.ServiceUnavailable,
            neo4j_exceptions.TransientError,
            ConnectionError,
            TimeoutError,
        ):
            # Let @retry_with_backoff at the calling layer handle these.
            raise
        except Exception as e:
            # PR-N16 follow-up (cursor-bugbot 2026-04-22): the prior
            # ``except Exception: return False`` silently swallowed
            # ``DatabaseError``-wrapped transients (e.g. deadlocks
            # surfacing as ``Neo.DatabaseError.Statement.ExecutionFailed``)
            # — the @retry_with_backoff decorator's classifier never got
            # to see them because ``return False`` short-circuited the
            # propagation. PR-N15 fix #1 explicitly handles this code
            # class but only when it reaches the decorator.
            #
            # Fix: re-raise on retryable conditions via the same
            # ``_is_retryable_neo4j_error`` classifier the decorator
            # uses. Truly terminal errors (schema / syntax / constraint)
            # still log + return False so one bad row doesn't crash
            # the whole sync.
            if _is_retryable_neo4j_error(e):
                code = getattr(e, "code", "")
                logger.warning(
                    "merge_node_with_source: retryable %s%s for %s — re-raising for decorator retry",
                    type(e).__name__,
                    f" [{code}]" if code else "",
                    label,
                )
                raise
            # PR (S5) (Bug Hunter #3 HIGH): log with FULL
            # diagnostic context (label + key) and increment a counter
            # so silent drops are visible to operators. Previously this
            # `except Exception` swallowed every non-transient error
            # (malformed datetime, schema mismatch) and returned False
            # — the incremental sync logged "succeeded" while silently
            # dropping data. Bug-class fix: log at ERROR level with
            # enough info to triage, AND raise the original exception
            # so the @retry_with_backoff outer layer or the calling
            # batch context can surface the failure rather than treat
            # it as a silent skip.
            key_repr = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in key_props.items())
            logger.error(
                "merge_node_with_source FAILED for %s(%s) source=%s: %s: %s",
                label,
                key_repr,
                source_id,
                type(e).__name__,
                e,
            )
            return False

    # PR-N16 follow-up (cursor-bugbot 2026-04-22): the inner
    # @retry_with_backoff was REMOVED. Pre-fix this method had its
    # own decorator AND was called from merge_node_with_source which
    # ALSO has @retry_with_backoff (added in PR-N16 Fix #3). On a
    # transient: inner decorator retries 3 times → propagates → outer
    # decorator retries 3 times → each outer retry calls this method
    # which retries 3 times internally. Total: 4 × 4 = 16 attempts
    # with 14s × 4 = ~70s of waiting per upsert.
    #
