    # Now: only the outer @retry_with_backoff on merge_node_with_source
    # retries (4 attempts, ~14s max waiting). _upsert_sourced_relationship
    # is private and only called from merge_node_with_source, so
    # removing the inner decorator is safe — exception classification
    # happens at the outer level via _is_retryable_neo4j_error.
    def _upsert_sourced_relationship(
        self,
        label: str,
        key_props: Dict,
        source_id: str,
        raw_data_json: str,
        confidence: float,
        source_reported_first_at: Optional[str] = None,
        source_reported_last_at: Optional[str] = None,
        misp_event_id: Optional[str] = None,
        source_refs: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        report: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        zones: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        stated_zones: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        stated_refs: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        refresh_raw_data: bool = False,
    ) -> bool:
        """Create or update SOURCED_FROM relationship with raw data + per-source
        timestamps on the edge.

        2026-10 (source revisions): ``r.raw_data`` is written when the edge is created and, with
        ``refresh_raw_data`` (a CVE write from a MISP attribute, ``merge_cve``), replaced on every write,
        so the edge of a CVE holds its source's latest record: a KEV or NVD copy edited in MISP reaches
        the edge at the next sync. Other labels, and the CVE write of the opt-in STIX import (a reduced
        record, not the source's), keep the record that created the edge.

        2026-10-16 (sector evidence): the edge accumulates the zones this source's records gave the node
        (``r.zones``), the part of them the source stated itself (``r.stated_zones``) and which record
        stated which zone (``r.stated_refs``), so a link to a Sector names only the feeds that gave its
        sector and cites only the records that gave it (``_sourced_zone_items``).

        2026-10-16 (indicator aging): ``report`` (an Indicator write only, ``indicator_aging.report_row``)
        records the source's report on the edge, forward only: ``r.last_recorded_at`` and, when the
        report is newer, ``r.last_reported_at`` / ``r.last_reported_ref`` / ``r.last_reported_source``
        (``indicator_aging.edge_report_items``).

        2026-10 (relationship provenance): the edge also accumulates, per source, the
        MISP events that carried this entity (``r.misp_event_ids``) and the source's own
        record ids for it (``r.source_refs``, ``"<feed>:<id>"``). ``build_relationships``
        copies both onto the links it derives from this node, so a built link traces
        back to the feed record and the MISP event like a link the sync writes directly.

        PR (S5) (architecture redesign — user-driven): source-
        reported timestamps live HERE, on the per-source edge, NOT on the
        node. Rationale: a single Indicator may be reported by multiple
        sources (NVD, AbuseIPDB, ThreatFox), each with its own
        first/last-reported claim. Aggregating to the node-level via
        MIN/MAX hides the per-source provenance — the consumer can no
        longer answer "what did NVD specifically say vs ThreatFox?".
        Per-source claims live on the per-source edge. The node carries
        only DB-local truths (``n.first_imported_at`` /
        ``n.last_updated``) — facts about EdgeGuard's own observation
        history that cannot be misread as real-world claims.

        Edge property contract (mirrors the node-level pattern but
        scoped to one source):

        - ``r.imported_at`` (existing): when EdgeGuard first saw THIS
          source report this entity. ON CREATE SET only; never
          overwritten. DB-local fact, per-source.
        - ``r.updated_at`` (existing): when EdgeGuard last saw THIS
          source report it. Refreshed on every MERGE = ``datetime()``.
          DB-local fact, per-source.
        - ``r.source_reported_first_at`` (NEW): the source's own claim
          about when it FIRST recorded this entity (NVD ``published``,
          CISA ``dateAdded``, AbuseIPDB ``firstSeen``, ThreatFox
          ``first_seen``, MITRE ``created``). Optional — NULL when the
          source isn't on the reliable allowlist. **MIN semantics on
          update**: if a stale import or a source backdate-correction
          arrives, we keep the earliest claim. Stale imports cannot
          regress because MIN-with-AND-guard rejects newer values.
        - ``r.source_reported_last_at`` (NEW): the source's own claim
          about when it LAST recorded this entity. Optional. **MAX
          semantics on update**: latest source observation wins.

        Returns:
            True if successful
        """
        if not self.driver:
            return False

        _validate_label(label)
        for k in key_props:
            _validate_prop_name(k)
        key_conditions = " AND ".join([f"n.{k} = ${k}" for k in key_props.keys()])
        # The Source node is keyed by the canonical id; an alias writes to it (``SOURCES`` above).
        source_id = source_registry.canonical_source_id(source_id) or source_id

        # Endpoint uuids — same canonicalization as the actual node MERGEs, so
        # r.src_uuid/r.trg_uuid resolve back to (label, key_props) and (Source, source_id).
        src_uuid, trg_uuid = edge_endpoint_uuids(label, key_props, "Source", {"source_id": source_id})

        # The MIN/MAX CASE clauses use the same defensive pattern as the
        # batch MERGEs:
        #   - AND-guard against NULL incoming (don't overwrite existing
        #     non-NULL with NULL aggregate)
        #   - datetime() wrapper on the parameter so the comparison is
        #     between two native Neo4j DateTime types (no string-vs-DateTime
        #     mix; pinned by tests/test_first_seen_at_source.py)
        query = f"""
        MATCH (n:{label})
        WHERE {key_conditions}
        MATCH (s:Source {{source_id: $source_id}})
        MERGE (n)-[r:SOURCED_FROM]->(s)
        ON CREATE SET r.imported_at = datetime(),
            r.raw_data = $raw_data,
            r.src_uuid = $src_uuid,
            r.trg_uuid = $trg_uuid,
            r.source_reported_first_at = CASE WHEN $source_reported_first_at IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE datetime($source_reported_first_at) END,
            r.source_reported_last_at = CASE WHEN $source_reported_last_at IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE datetime($source_reported_last_at) END
        SET r.confidence = $confidence,
            r.source = $source_id,
            r.misp_event_ids = {_dedup_concat_optional_clause("r.misp_event_ids", "$misp_event_id", require_nonempty_string=True)},
            r.source_refs = {_dedup_concat_clause("r.source_refs", "coalesce($source_refs, [])")},
            {_sourced_zone_items("r", "$zones", "$stated_zones", "$stated_refs")},
            r.updated_at = datetime(),
            r.edgeguard_managed = true,
            r.src_uuid = coalesce(r.src_uuid, $src_uuid),
            r.trg_uuid = coalesce(r.trg_uuid, $trg_uuid),
            // PR (S5) (Red Team v2 M3 + Bug Hunter v2 #10):
            // use NESTED CASE rather than ``AND``-combined predicate.
            // Cypher's AND is a value operator, not short-circuit
            // control flow — so ``$X IS NOT NULL AND datetime($X) < r.X``
            // may evaluate ``datetime(NULL)`` (which returns NULL and
            // makes the AND falsy, so behavior is correct today —
            // but it's working by accident). Nested CASE makes the
            // short-circuit explicit and survives future Cypher
            // parser / optimizer changes.
            r.source_reported_first_at = CASE
                WHEN $source_reported_first_at IS NULL THEN r.source_reported_first_at
                WHEN r.source_reported_first_at IS NULL THEN datetime($source_reported_first_at)
                WHEN datetime($source_reported_first_at) < r.source_reported_first_at
                    THEN datetime($source_reported_first_at)
                ELSE r.source_reported_first_at
            END,
            r.source_reported_last_at = CASE
                WHEN $source_reported_last_at IS NULL THEN r.source_reported_last_at
                WHEN r.source_reported_last_at IS NULL THEN datetime($source_reported_last_at)
                WHEN datetime($source_reported_last_at) > r.source_reported_last_at
                    THEN datetime($source_reported_last_at)
                ELSE r.source_reported_last_at
            END"""
        if refresh_raw_data:
            query += """,
            r.raw_data = $raw_data"""
        if report is not None:
            query += f""",
            {edge_report_items("r", "$report", "$source_id")}"""

        try:
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                params = {
                    **key_props,
                    "source_id": source_id,
                    "raw_data": raw_data_json,
                    "confidence": confidence,
                    "src_uuid": src_uuid,
                    "trg_uuid": trg_uuid,
                    "source_reported_first_at": source_reported_first_at,
                    "source_reported_last_at": source_reported_last_at,
                    "misp_event_id": str(misp_event_id) if misp_event_id else None,
                    "source_refs": [str(x) for x in (source_refs or []) if x],
                    "zones": _zone_param(zones),
                    "stated_zones": _zone_param(stated_zones) or [],
                    "stated_refs": _zone_param(stated_refs) or [],
                }
                if report is not None:
                    params["report"] = dict(report)
                session.run(query, **params, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT).consume()
            return True
        except (
            neo4j_exceptions.ServiceUnavailable,
            neo4j_exceptions.TransientError,
            ConnectionError,
            TimeoutError,
        ):
            raise  # let outer @retry_with_backoff (on merge_node_with_source) handle transient errors
        except Exception as e:
            # PR-N16 follow-up #3 (cursor-bugbot 2026-04-22):
            # ``except Exception: return False`` was swallowing
            # ``DatabaseError``-wrapped transients (the exact error
            # class PR-N16 Fix #3 targets). After removing the inner
            # @retry_with_backoff (follow-up #2, to avoid nested retry
            # stacking), the OUTER decorator on merge_node_with_source
            # can only retry if this inner method propagates the
            # exception. Swallowing + return False short-circuits that.
            #
            # Fix: use the same _is_retryable_neo4j_error classifier +
            # re-raise pattern as merge_node_with_source. Terminal
            # errors (schema / syntax / constraint) still log + return
            # False so one bad row doesn't crash the calling sync.
            if _is_retryable_neo4j_error(e):
                code = getattr(e, "code", "")
                logger.warning(
                    "_upsert_sourced_relationship: retryable %s%s for %s — re-raising for outer decorator retry",
                    type(e).__name__,
                    f" [{code}]" if code else "",
                    label,
                )
                raise
            # 2026-10-16: name the node and the source, as ``merge_node_with_source FAILED`` does.
            # Since the result is read here, an execution error of this statement (a source timestamp
            # the server cannot convert, for one) reaches this line, and merge_node_with_source
            # returns this False without a line of its own.
            key_repr = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in key_props.items())
            logger.warning(
                "SOURCED_FROM relationship error (terminal) for %s(%s) source=%s: %s: %s",
                label,
                key_repr,
                source_id,
                type(e).__name__,
                e,
            )
            return False

    def merge_vulnerability(self, data: Dict, source_id: str = "nvd") -> bool:
        """MERGE a Vulnerability node with source tracking."""
        cve_id = resolve_vulnerability_cve_id(data)
        if not cve_id:
            logger.warning(
                "merge_vulnerability: missing resolvable cve_id (expected cve_id or type=vulnerability with value)"
            )
            return False
        data = dict(data)
        data["cve_id"] = cve_id
        key_props = {"cve_id": cve_id}
        extra_props: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        if data.get("cvss_score") is not None:
            extra_props["cvss_score"] = data["cvss_score"]
        if data.get("severity"):
            extra_props["severity"] = data["severity"]
        if data.get("attack_vector"):
            extra_props["attack_vector"] = data["attack_vector"]
        # PR-N20 follow-up to PR-N19 Fix #1: preserve symmetry with
        # ``merge_cve``. The single-row NVD path (``merge_vulnerability``)
        # is used by alert-pipeline callers and the ``_sync_single_item``
        # fallback; the batch path (``merge_vulnerabilities_batch``) writes
        # dates via SOURCED_FROM edges, but the node itself would drop
        # ``published`` / ``last_modified`` without this promotion — exactly
        # the same bug shape PR-N19 Fix #1 closed for ``merge_cve``.
        # 2026-10: dates as in ``merge_cve`` — set by NVD's record, filled by any other; the description
        # by the source ranking (2026-10-16).
        fill_props: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        record_dates = extra_props if data.get("nvd_record") else fill_props
        for prop in _CVE_RECORD_DATE_PROPS:
            if data.get(prop):
                record_dates[prop] = data[prop]
        return self.merge_node_with_source(
            "Vulnerability",
            key_props,
            data,
            source_id,
            extra_props=extra_props or None,
            fill_props=fill_props or None,
            description=CVE_DESCRIPTIONS.record(data.get("description"), source_id),
        )

    def merge_indicator(self, data: Dict, source_id: str = "alienvault_otx") -> bool:
        """MERGE an Indicator node with source tracking.

        PR #37 commit X (bugbot HIGH): the natural-key value is canonicalized
        via ``canonicalize_merge_key`` BEFORE the MERGE, matching the
        treatment in ``merge_indicators_batch`` and ``merge_malware``/
        ``merge_actor``. Without this, indicators arriving through the
        single-item path (VirusTotal enrichment, STIX pipeline import,
        ``_sync_single_item`` fallback) retained original casing in the
        Cypher MERGE while UUID was computed case-insensitively → two
        Neo4j nodes sharing ONE uuid. The audit-driven batch fix was
        applied in PR #37 commit 3 but the single-item path was missed
        — bugbot caught it.

        PR-N13 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit Fix #1): reject None /
        empty / whitespace-only ``value`` or ``indicator_type`` at
        entry. The prior code let ``{"indicator_type": None, "value":
        None}`` reach the Cypher MERGE, which collapses every None-
        keyed row into ONE sentinel Indicator node. A single malformed
        OTX pulse emitting ``{"type": "ipv4", "indicator": ""}`` can
        therefore poison a production hub node that every subsequent
        empty row cross-joins to. Mirror of ``merge_ip`` / ``merge_host``
        None-guards (already established pattern).
        """
        norm_value = nonempty_graph_string(data.get("value"))
        norm_type = nonempty_graph_string(data.get("indicator_type"))
        if norm_value is None or norm_type is None:
            logger.warning(
                "[MERGE-REJECT] Indicator MERGE refused: indicator_type=%r value=%r "
                "(one or both are None / empty / whitespace-only). Creating a "
                "null-keyed Indicator would produce a sentinel hub node that "
                "every subsequent empty-keyed row collapses into.",
                data.get("indicator_type"),
                data.get("value"),
            )
            return False
        key_props = canonicalize_merge_key(
            "Indicator",
            {
                "indicator_type": norm_type,
                "value": norm_value,
            },
        )
        # Promote enrichment fields to queryable node properties
        extra_props: Dict = {}
        if data.get("attack_ids"):
            extra_props["attack_ids"] = data["attack_ids"]
        if data.get("targeted_countries"):
            extra_props["targeted_countries"] = data["targeted_countries"]
        if data.get("malware_family"):
            extra_props["malware_family"] = data["malware_family"]
        if data.get("malware_malpedia"):
            extra_props["malware_malpedia"] = data["malware_malpedia"]
        if data.get("reference"):
            extra_props["reference"] = data["reference"]
        if data.get("reporter"):
            extra_props["reporter"] = data["reporter"]
        if data.get("domain"):
            extra_props["domain"] = data["domain"]
        if data.get("hostnames"):
            extra_props["hostnames"] = data["hostnames"]
        return self.merge_node_with_source("Indicator", key_props, data, source_id, extra_props=extra_props or None)

    def merge_cve(self, data: Dict, source_id: str = "nvd", *, refresh_raw_data: bool = True) -> bool:
        """
        MERGE a CVE node with source tracking, then create CVSS sub-nodes.

        After merging the CVE, creates CVSS sub-nodes (v4.0 / v3.1 / v3.0 / v2) when
        ``cvss_v40_data`` / ``cvss_v31_data`` / ``cvss_v30_data`` / ``cvss_v2_data`` are present,
        with matching ``HAS_CVSS_*`` relationships (ResilMesh schema), then sets the node's
        ``cvss_score`` / ``severity`` / ``cvss_version`` / ``attack_vector`` from those sub-nodes
        (2026-10; the record's own ``cvss_score`` / ``severity`` / ``attack_vector`` are not written).
        ``published`` and ``last_modified`` are set by NVD's record (``nvd_record``) and only filled,
        where the node has none, by any other record (2026-10); so are ``cwe``, ``ref_tags``,
        ``cpe_type``, ``result_impacts``, ``reference_urls`` and ``affected_products`` (2026-10, a
        record of the NVD source counting as NVD's), and a CVSS sub-node NVD has asserted keeps NVD's
        payload (``_merge_cvss_node``). ``description`` and
        ``description_source`` follow the source ranking NVD > CISA KEV > CISA ICS > any other source
        (``description_ranking.CVE_DESCRIPTIONS``, 2026-10-16). ``cisa_exploit_add``,
        ``cisa_action_due``, ``cisa_required_action`` and ``cisa_vulnerability_name`` are set by a CISA
        KEV record and only filled by any other (``_KEV_OWNED_CVE_PROPS``, 2026-10). The
        ``SOURCED_FROM`` edge's ``raw_data`` is replaced with the record on every write (2026-10), so
        the edge holds the source's latest record; ``refresh_raw_data=False`` writes it only when the
        edge is created, for a caller whose record is not the source's (the STIX import of
        ``run_pipeline``, a reduced record under the MISP event's source id).

        Returns False when the node's MERGE or one of the sub-writes (CVSS sub-nodes, NVD-owned data,
        score) fails with a terminal error (2026-10); a retryable error that outlasts its retries is
        raised.
        """
        cve_id = resolve_vulnerability_cve_id(data)
        if not cve_id:
            logger.warning("merge_cve: missing resolvable cve_id (expected cve_id or type=vulnerability with value)")
            return False
        data = dict(data)
        data["cve_id"] = cve_id
        key_props = {"cve_id": cve_id}

        # Promote CISA KEV fields to queryable node properties so analysts
        # can filter on e.g. "all CVEs on the CISA KEV list".
        #
        # PR #34 round 18: deleted ``reference_urls`` from extra_props.
        # The NVD collector parses up to 10 advisory URLs per CVE and
        # forwards them here, but ZERO consumers downstream
        # (no GraphQL field, no STIX export, no Cypher query). Same
        # dead-write pattern as round-17's ``original_*_date`` cleanup.
        extra_props: Dict = {}
        fill_props: Dict = {}
        # 2026-10: the KEV record owns its four fields. A CISA KEV record sets them; any other record
        # (NVD's carries the same four from its own KEV enrichment) only fills them where the node has
        # none. Before, the record merged last set them, and NVD's copy can hold an older value: NVD did
        # not move ``lastModified`` when CISA moved the due date of CVE-2022-0995 (2026-10-08), so NVD's
        # MISP copy kept the old date and a sync that read it after the KEV record wrote it back.
        kev_owned = extra_props if source_registry.canonical_source_id(source_id) == "cisa_kev" else fill_props
        for prop in _KEV_OWNED_CVE_PROPS:
            if data.get(prop):
                kev_owned[prop] = data[prop]
        # 2026-10: CISA's ``knownRansomwareCampaignUse`` ("Known" / "Unknown"), carried by the KEV
        # collector's records only, so an NVD record never overwrites it.
        if data.get("known_ransomware_use"):
            extra_props["known_ransomware_use"] = str(data["known_ransomware_use"])
        # 2026-10: ``cvss_score``, ``severity`` and ``attack_vector`` are not taken from the record —
        # they are derived from the CVSS sub-nodes below (``_set_cve_score_from_cvss``). The record's
        # values were whatever its source sent: a 0.0 placeholder read back as 3.0 / LOW, a
        # ransomware-derived KEV value, "UNKNOWN" from a source without scores, a vector-string
        # letter ("N") from NVD or an invented "NETWORK" from KEV and OTX, and the last record merged won.
        # PR-N19 Fix #1 (post-baseline 2026-04-22, from Bravo's
        # baseline-run audit): promote NVD ``published`` +
        # ``last_modified`` to node properties. Pre-PR-N19 the data
        # was correctly rehydrated from NVD_META into
        # ``item["published"]`` / ``item["last_modified"]``
        # (``run_misp_to_neo4j.py:2487-2488``) but this extra_props
        # builder never included them — so ``c.published`` and
        # ``c.last_modified`` stayed NULL on every NVD CVE. Only
        # ``c.first_imported_at`` (the EdgeGuard DB-local fact) had
        # a date. The ResilMesh-native ``merge_resilmesh_cve`` at
        # L5051 correctly writes both; the MISP-sourced path (the
        # one used for the 99,664 CVEs in the 2026-04-22 baseline)
        # did not. Fixes the gap Bravo caught.
        # 2026-10: ``published`` and ``last_modified`` are set by NVD's record only (``nvd_record``, set
        # by the sync for an NVD attribute with NVD_META); any other record fills them where the node has
        # none (``_CVE_RECORD_DATE_PROPS``). Before, the record merged last set them, and the description
        # with them, so a CVE showed OTX's raw pulse JSON, a pulse name or CISA's short text instead of
        # NVD's description depending on the order of the events in the sync. 2026-10-16: the description
        # follows the source ranking (``description_ranking``), so on a CVE without NVD's record the
        # KEV's text wins over CISA ICS's, and CISA ICS's over any other, in any order.
        record_dates = extra_props if data.get("nvd_record") else fill_props
        for prop in _CVE_RECORD_DATE_PROPS:
            if data.get(prop):
                record_dates[prop] = data[prop]
        # 2026-10 (fresh-baseline PR, ResilMesh conformance finding F2): the four
        # ResilMesh CVE properties ``cwe``, ``ref_tags``, ``cpe_type`` and
        # ``result_impacts`` were rehydrated from NVD_META into the item but never
        # promoted to the node by this path (only the batch Vulnerability path and
        # ``merge_resilmesh_cve`` wrote them), so every CVE in the 2026-09 baseline
        # had them only inside ``SOURCED_FROM.raw_data``. ``reference_urls`` and
        # ``affected_products`` ride along for parity with the batch path (CPE
        # strings are what a vendor/product sector rule needs).
        # 2026-10: like the dates, NVD's record sets the lists and any other record only fills a list the
        # node does not have. Before, the record merged last set them, so a CISA ICS record merged after
        # NVD's replaced NVD's CPE strings with product names, NVD's references with the advisory's URL
        # and NVD's CWE with CISA's. Of the other records only CISA ICS gives these lists, from one
        # attribute per CVE in MISP, so the result does not depend on the order. An item of the NVD
        # source without ``nvd_record`` counts as NVD's record (the lists come only with ``NVD_META``).
        from_nvd = bool(data.get("nvd_record")) or source_registry.canonical_source_id(source_id) == "nvd"
        record_lists = extra_props if from_nvd else fill_props
        for _list_prop in ("cwe", "ref_tags", "cpe_type", "result_impacts", "reference_urls", "affected_products"):
            _val = data.get(_list_prop)
            if isinstance(_val, list) and _val:
                _clean = [str(x) for x in _val if x is not None and str(x) != ""]
                if _clean:  # never overwrite an existing list with an empty one
                    record_lists[_list_prop] = _clean
        # 2026-10: NVD's record status (``["rejected"]`` or ``["active"]``, from ``NVD_META``) on the
        # node, replaced on every write so a rejection that arrives with an update reaches the graph.
        # Before, it stayed in ``SOURCED_FROM.raw_data`` only (0 of 141,730 CVE nodes had it on
        # 2026-10-14; 3,963 were rejected). Written only when the item carries one: CISA and OTX CVE
        # items do not, so they cannot reset it.
        _status = data.get("status")
        if isinstance(_status, list):
            _status_clean = [str(x) for x in _status if x is not None and str(x) != ""]
            if _status_clean:
                extra_props["status"] = _status_clean

        ok = self.merge_node_with_source(
            "CVE",
            key_props,
            data,
            source_id,
            extra_props=extra_props or None,
            fill_props=fill_props or None,
            description=CVE_DESCRIPTIONS.record(data.get("description"), source_id),
            # 2026-10: the SOURCED_FROM edge holds the source's latest record (an edited MISP copy
            # re-read by the sync), not the record that created the edge.
            refresh_raw_data=refresh_raw_data,
        )
        if not ok:
            return False
        # 2026-10: each sub-write retries a retryable error and raises it once its retries are spent; a
        # terminal error makes it return False, the remaining sub-writes still run, and merge_cve returns
        # False, so the sync counts the CVE as an error. Before, the three helpers logged every error at
        # WARNING, retryable ones included, and the CVE counted as synced.
        failed_sub_writes = 0
        # Create CVSS sub-nodes (ResilMesh schema)
        tag = data.get("tag", "default")
        for label, rel_type, key in (
            ("CVSSv40", "HAS_CVSS_v40", "cvss_v40_data"),
            ("CVSSv31", "HAS_CVSS_v31", "cvss_v31_data"),
            ("CVSSv30", "HAS_CVSS_v30", "cvss_v30_data"),
            ("CVSSv2", "HAS_CVSS_v2", "cvss_v2_data"),
        ):
            if data.get(key) and not self._merge_cvss_node(
                cve_id, tag, label, rel_type, data[key], misp_event_id=data.get("misp_event_id")
            ):
                failed_sub_writes += 1
        if data.get("nvd_record") and not self._replace_nvd_owned_cve_data(cve_id, data):
            failed_sub_writes += 1
        # Last step: any code that adds or removes CVSS sub-nodes of this CVE must run before it,
        # or the node keeps a score derived from sub-nodes that no longer apply.
        if not self._set_cve_score_from_cvss(cve_id):
            failed_sub_writes += 1
        return failed_sub_writes == 0

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def _replace_nvd_owned_cve_data(self, cve_id: str, data: Dict) -> bool:
        """Remove from the node what NVD's record no longer has (2026-10).

        For an NVD record read from MISP (``nvd_record``, set by the sync when the attribute carries
        ``NVD_META``). ``merge_cve`` never overwrites a list with an empty one and never removes a CVSS
        sub-node, so data NVD withdrew (a rejection, a removed CWE, CVSS or CPE) would otherwise stay
        from an earlier record:

        - the lists ``cwe``, ``ref_tags``, ``cpe_type``, ``result_impacts``, ``reference_urls`` and
          ``affected_products`` are set from the record even when empty (an empty list removes the
          property), but only on a node EdgeGuard manages whose only source is NVD. CISA ICS, the KEV
          and OTX records and partner writes supply these lists as well, and on such a node an empty
          NVD list leaves them as they are (on the hosted graph of 2026-10-14, 126,669 of the CVE
          nodes with ``cwe`` had NVD as their only source);
        - a CVSS sub-node of a version the record no longer has is removed when EdgeGuard manages it
          and NVD is the only feed that asserted it (``sources`` of its ``HAS_CVSS_*`` edge, or the
          node's ``tag`` where the edge predates ``sources``): CISA ICS writes CVSS sub-nodes too. On
          a sub-node another feed also asserted, NVD is taken out of ``sources`` and the record's event
          out of ``misp_event_ids`` of both edges (2026-10), as a rebuild from the same records gives:
          the sub-node no longer counts as NVD's (``_merge_cvss_node``), so the other feed's next
          record sets its payload. Until that record the sub-node keeps the values it has, NVD's;
          before, NVD stayed in ``sources``, and the other feed's records only filled the sub-node;
        - CISA's SSVC decision points (``ssvc_exploitation``, ``ssvc_automatable``,
          ``ssvc_technical_impact``, with ``ssvc_version`` and ``ssvc_timestamp``; 2026-10) are set
          from the record on any node, and removed when the record has none: no other source supplies
          them, so a decision CISA changed or withdrew never stays from an earlier record.

        A retryable error is retried and then raised, a terminal one logged and returned as False, which
        ``merge_cve`` returns (``_cve_sub_write_failed``, 2026-10); either leaves the node as it was.
        """
        if not self.driver or not cve_id:
            return False
        lists: Dict[str, Optional[List[str]]] = {}
        for prop in _NVD_OWNED_CVE_LISTS:
            value = data.get(prop)
            clean = [str(x) for x in value if x is not None and str(x) != ""] if isinstance(value, list) else []
            lists[prop] = clean or None
        absent = [rel_type for rel_type, key in _NVD_CVSS_VERSIONS if not data.get(key)]
        ssvc = _nvd_ssvc_values(data.get("ssvc"))
        set_clause = ", ".join(
            [f"c.{prop} = CASE WHEN nvd_only THEN ${prop} ELSE c.{prop} END" for prop in _NVD_OWNED_CVE_LISTS]
            + [f"c.{prop} = ${prop}" for prop in ssvc]
        )
        query = f"""
        MATCH (c:CVE {{cve_id: $cve_id}})
        WITH c, (c.edgeguard_managed = true AND coalesce(c.source, []) = ['nvd']) AS nvd_only
        SET {set_clause}
        WITH c
        OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[r:HAS_CVSS_v40|HAS_CVSS_v31|HAS_CVSS_v30|HAS_CVSS_v2]->(s)
        WHERE type(r) IN $absent_rel_types AND s.cve_id = $cve_id AND s.edgeguard_managed = true
          AND coalesce(r.sources, [s.tag]) = ['nvd']
        DETACH DELETE s
        WITH DISTINCT c
        OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[r:HAS_CVSS_v40|HAS_CVSS_v31|HAS_CVSS_v30|HAS_CVSS_v2]-(s)
        WHERE type(r) IN $absent_rel_types AND s.cve_id = $cve_id
          AND 'nvd' IN r.sources AND any(feed IN r.sources WHERE feed <> 'nvd')
        SET r.sources = [feed IN r.sources WHERE feed <> 'nvd'],
            r.misp_event_ids = [event IN r.misp_event_ids WHERE event <> $nvd_event_id]
        """
        try:
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                session.run(
                    query,
                    cve_id=cve_id,
                    absent_rel_types=absent,
                    nvd_event_id=str(data.get("misp_event_id") or ""),
                    **lists,
                    **ssvc,
                    timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT,
                ).consume()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            return _cve_sub_write_failed(e, f"Failed to replace the NVD data of CVE {cve_id}")

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def _set_cve_score_from_cvss(self, cve_id: str) -> bool:
        """Set the CVE node's ``cvss_score`` / ``severity`` / ``cvss_version`` / ``attack_vector``
        from its CVSS sub-nodes (v3.1 → v3.0 → v2 → v4.0); no CVSS → null score, version and attack
        vector, severity UNKNOWN. The attack vector is that of the sub-node that gives the score,
        in NVD's words (``cvss_selection.payload_attack_vector``).

        Runs after every ``merge_cve`` (2026-10), whichever source the record came from, so a
        record without CVSS (OTX, KEV, an NVD record awaiting analysis) cannot erase another
        source's score and a CVSS 3.1 from CISA ICS outranks NVD's CVSS 4.0. A retryable error is
        retried and then raised, a terminal one logged and returned as False (``_cve_sub_write_failed``,
        2026-10); either leaves the previous values.
        """
        if not self.driver or not cve_id:
            return False
        try:
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                session.run(_CVE_SCORE_FROM_CVSS_QUERY, cve_id=cve_id, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT).consume()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            return _cve_sub_write_failed(e, f"Failed to set the CVSS score of CVE {cve_id}")

    @retry_with_backoff(max_retries=3)
    def _merge_cvss_node(
        self,
        cve_id: str,
        tag: str,
        label: str,
        rel_type: str,
        cvss_data: Dict,
        misp_event_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        MERGE a CVSS sub-node (v2 / v3.0 / v3.1 / v4.0) and link it to its parent CVE.

        Implements the ResilMesh schema, e.g.:
          [CVE]-[:HAS_CVSS_v31]->[CVSSv31 {...}]
          [CVE]-[:HAS_CVSS_v30]->[CVSSv30 {...}]
          [CVE]-[:HAS_CVSS_v2]->[CVSSv2 {...}]

        Both HAS_CVSS_v* edges are stamped with src_uuid/trg_uuid (the CVE's
        and the CVSS sub-node's deterministic uuids) for cross-environment
        traceability and self-describing edge serialization.

        2026-10 (relationship provenance): both edges also name the feed that
        delivered the score (``r.sources``, the CVE's source tag, normally ``nvd``)
        and the MISP event that carried it (``r.misp_event_ids``).

        2026-10 (NVD precedence): one sub-node per CVE and version holds NVD's and CISA ICS's
        score alike. Once NVD has asserted it (``'nvd'`` in ``sources`` of the CVE's edge to it,
        or the node's ``tag`` where the edge predates ``sources``), another feed's payload only
        fills a property the node lacks (``_set_if_absent_clause``), so the node holds NVD's payload
        whatever the order of the records; NVD's own write and a write to a sub-node only other
        feeds asserted set the payload. ``r.sources`` and ``r.misp_event_ids`` still name every feed
        and event. An edge that predates ``sources`` gets the feed the guard read from the node's
        ``tag`` (``_cvss_legacy_sources_cypher``) before the writing feed is added, so a sub-node NVD
        asserted that way stays NVD's on the next write too; a new edge names the writing feed only.
        Before, every write set its whole payload and the record merged last won. An NVD
        record without the version takes NVD out of ``sources`` (``_replace_nvd_owned_cve_data``), so
        the other feed's next write sets its payload again.

        A retryable error is retried and then raised, a terminal one logged and returned as False,
        which ``merge_cve`` returns (``_cve_sub_write_failed``, 2026-10).
        """
        if not self.driver or not cve_id:
            return False
        try:
            _validate_label(label)
            _validate_rel_type(rel_type)

            # Build SET clause dynamically from the cvss_data dict.
            # Filter out None/empty values to avoid setting properties to NULL.
            filtered_cvss = {k: v for k, v in cvss_data.items() if v is not None and v != ""}
            prop_assignments = []
            for k in filtered_cvss:
                _validate_prop_name(k)
                prop_assignments.append(
                    f"n.{k} = CASE WHEN nvd_owned THEN {_set_if_absent_clause(f'n.{k}', f'${k}')} ELSE ${k} END"
                )
            set_clause = ", ".join(prop_assignments) if prop_assignments else "n.created = true"

            cve_uuid = compute_node_uuid("CVE", {"cve_id": cve_id})
            cvss_uuid = compute_node_uuid(label, {"cve_id": cve_id})

            query = f"""
            MATCH (cve:CVE {{cve_id: $cve_id}})
            MERGE (n:{label} {{cve_id: $cve_id}})
            ON CREATE SET n.uuid = $cvss_uuid, n.edgeguard_managed = true
            ON MATCH SET n.edgeguard_enriched = CASE WHEN n.edgeguard_managed = true THEN n.edgeguard_enriched ELSE true END
            WITH cve, n, {_cvss_legacy_sources_cypher("n")} AS legacy_sources
            WITH cve, n, legacy_sources, ($feed <> 'nvd' AND EXISTS {{
                MATCH (cve)-[x:{rel_type}]->(n) WHERE 'nvd' IN coalesce(x.sources, legacy_sources)
            }}) AS nvd_owned
            SET {set_clause},
                n.tag = coalesce(n.tag, $tag),
                n.last_updated = datetime(),
                n.uuid = coalesce(n.uuid, $cvss_uuid)
            MERGE (cve)-[r1:{rel_type}]->(n)
                ON CREATE SET r1.src_uuid = $cve_uuid, r1.trg_uuid = $cvss_uuid
                ON MATCH SET r1.sources = coalesce(r1.sources, legacy_sources)
            SET r1.src_uuid = coalesce(r1.src_uuid, $cve_uuid),
                r1.trg_uuid = coalesce(r1.trg_uuid, $cvss_uuid),
                r1.edgeguard_managed = true,
                r1.sources = {_dedup_concat_clause("r1.sources", "[$feed]")},
                r1.misp_event_ids = {_dedup_concat_optional_clause("r1.misp_event_ids", "$misp_event_id", require_nonempty_string=True)}
            MERGE (n)-[r2:{rel_type}]->(cve)
                ON CREATE SET r2.src_uuid = $cvss_uuid, r2.trg_uuid = $cve_uuid
                ON MATCH SET r2.sources = coalesce(r2.sources, legacy_sources)
            SET r2.src_uuid = coalesce(r2.src_uuid, $cvss_uuid),
                r2.trg_uuid = coalesce(r2.trg_uuid, $cve_uuid),
                r2.edgeguard_managed = true,
                r2.sources = {_dedup_concat_clause("r2.sources", "[$feed]")},
                r2.misp_event_ids = {_dedup_concat_optional_clause("r2.misp_event_ids", "$misp_event_id", require_nonempty_string=True)}
            """
            # NB (PR #33 round 8, bugbot MED): spread filtered_cvss FIRST so the
            # explicit cve_uuid / cvss_uuid / cve_id / tag entries below always
            # win on key collision. If cvss_data ever contained a key named
            # ``cve_uuid`` or ``cvss_uuid`` (passes _validate_prop_name), a
            # later spread would silently overwrite the computed deterministic
            # uuids with attribute data.
            params = {
                **filtered_cvss,
                "cve_id": cve_id,
                "tag": tag,
                "cve_uuid": cve_uuid,
                "cvss_uuid": cvss_uuid,
                # ``tag`` falls back to "default" upstream when an item carries none.
                "feed": (source_registry.canonical_source_id(tag) if tag != "default" else None) or "misp",
                "misp_event_id": str(misp_event_id) if misp_event_id else None,
            }
            dropped = len(cvss_data) - len(filtered_cvss)
            with self.driver.session() as session:
                session.run(query, **params, timeout=NEO4J_READ_TIMEOUT).consume()
            logger.debug(
                "%s node merged for CVE %s (%s properties set, %s null/empty filtered)",
                label,
                cve_id,
                len(filtered_cvss),
                dropped,
            )
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            return _cve_sub_write_failed(e, f"Failed to merge {label} for CVE {cve_id}")

    def merge_malware(self, data: Dict, source_id: str = "alienvault_otx") -> bool:
        """MERGE a Malware node with source tracking.

        PR #37 (Logic Tracker Tier S): the natural-key ``name`` is now
        lowercase + NFC + stripped via ``canonicalize_merge_key`` BEFORE
        the MERGE. Without this, ``Malware{name:"TrickBot"}`` (OTX) and
        ``Malware{name:"trickbot"}`` (ThreatFox) became two distinct
        nodes that shared the SAME ``n.uuid`` (UUID computation already
        lowercases its hash input — see node_identity.py:340 — so the
        original Cypher-side case-sensitive MERGE was the only thing
        creating duplicates). Operators who relied on display case can
        recover the variant strings from ``n.aliases[]``.

        PR-N10 (2026-04-21 7-agent audit Bug Hunter P1, Red Team #1):
        reject MERGE when ``name`` canonicalizes to a placeholder
        sentinel like "unknown", "Unknown malware", "N/A", "none", etc.
        Three failure modes pre-fix:
          (1) Feeds emitting default ``"unknown"`` (VT fallback, OTX
              pulse-author fallback, MISPCollector meta-category
              fallback, ThreatFox malware_printable) create a single
              ``Malware{name:"unknown"}`` node. Q9 then links every
              Indicator with family="unknown" to it.
          (2) A compromised MISP peer (or low-privilege MISP user)
              creates ``Malware{name:"unknown", attributed_to:"APT29"}``.
              Q9 → thousands of false INDICATES; Q2 → false ATTRIBUTED_TO
              edge to real APT29 ThreatActor. Adversarial attribution.
          (3) ``build_campaign_nodes`` treats the placeholder-"unknown"
              Malware as a campaign anchor → false campaign absorbs
              indicators from dozens of unrelated threats.
        Defense-in-depth: Q2/Q9 Cypher WHERE also filter placeholders.

        ``description`` and ``description_source`` (2026-10-16): the source ranking MITRE ATT&CK > a curated
        source > any other source (``description_ranking.ENTITY_DESCRIPTIONS``); until then MITRE's record
        set the description and any other record only filled an empty one.
        """
        # PR-N10: reject placeholder names at ingest. Canonicalization
        # (NFC + strip + lower) happens inside is_placeholder_name so
        # "Unknown", "UNKNOWN", "  unknown  " all normalize identically.
        raw_name = data.get("name")
        if is_placeholder_name(raw_name):
            logger.warning(
                "[MERGE-REJECT] Malware name=%r is a placeholder sentinel — "
                "skipping MERGE. Source=%s. This is defense against feeds "
                "emitting 'unknown'/'N/A'/'Generic' as default names and "
                "against adversarial MISP attribution hijack (audit Bug "
                "Hunter P1, Red Team #1). See node_identity."
                "_REJECTED_PLACEHOLDER_NAMES for the full list.",
                raw_name,
                source_id,
            )
            # PR-N18 (2026-04-22): emit the counter PR-N11 promised.
            # Closes the log-grep-only detection path with proper
            # Prometheus alerting. None-guarded (PR-N5 R1 pattern).
            if _MERGE_REJECT_PLACEHOLDER is not None:
                try:
                    _MERGE_REJECT_PLACEHOLDER.labels(
                        label="Malware", source=source_registry.canonical_source_id(source_id) or source_id
                    ).inc()
                except Exception as _metric_err:
                    logger.debug("placeholder-reject metric increment failed: %s", _metric_err, exc_info=True)
            return False
        key_props = canonicalize_merge_key("Malware", {"name": raw_name})
        # Store malware types and aliases on the node for easier querying
        malware_types = data.get("malware_types", [])
        aliases = data.get("aliases", [])
        # MITRE ATT&CK STIX ``uses`` edges (technique IDs), via collector + MISP MITRE_USES_TECHNIQUES comment
        uses_techniques = data.get("uses_techniques", [])

        extra_props: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "malware_types": malware_types,
            "aliases": aliases,
            "uses_techniques": uses_techniques,
            # 2026-10: pulse-level technique ids (OTX) are kept apart from MITRE's
            # explicit list so build_relationships can label the edges honestly.
            "reported_techniques": data.get("reported_techniques", []) or [],
        }
        if data.get("pulse_id"):
            # Source-report provenance: every OTX pulse that mentioned this malware
            # (incl. the extra pulses de-duplication folded into ``report_ids``).
            extra_props["pulse_ids"] = [str(data["pulse_id"])] + [str(x) for x in (data.get("report_ids") or []) if x]
        # 2026-10: the record merged last used to set the description (an OTX pulse's text or a raw JSON
        # block among them); 2026-10-16: the source ranking decides (``description_ranking``).
        _mark_deprecated(data, extra_props)
        return self.merge_node_with_source(
            "Malware",
            key_props,
            data,
            source_id,
            extra_props=extra_props,
            description=ENTITY_DESCRIPTIONS.record(data.get("description"), source_id),
        )

    def merge_actor(self, data: Dict, source_id: str = "mitre_attck") -> bool:
        """MERGE a ThreatActor node with source tracking.

        PR #37: same ``canonicalize_merge_key`` treatment as ``merge_malware``
        — actor names like "APT29"/"apt29"/"Apt29" all merge into a single
        canonical lowercase node. Display-case variants are still
        recoverable via ``n.aliases[]``. (Note: this does NOT solve the
        actor-rename problem — e.g. APT29 → Cozy Bear → Midnight Blizzard
        — that's Tier A A1 and needs an alias-graph resolution pass,
        not just casing.)

        PR-N10: same placeholder-name reject as merge_malware. See that
        function's docstring for the full rationale. Without this guard,
        ``ThreatActor{name:"unknown"}`` becomes a false-hub to every
        Malware whose attributed_to is "unknown" / "unspecified" / etc.

        ``description`` and ``description_source``: as in ``merge_malware`` (2026-10-16).
        """
        raw_name = data.get("name")

            logger.warning(
                "[MERGE-REJECT] ThreatActor name=%r is a placeholder sentinel — "

                "rationale (PR-N10 audit Bug Hunter P3, Red Team #2).",
                raw_name,

            )
            # PR-N18 (2026-04-22): same counter emission as merge_malware.
            if _MERGE_REJECT_PLACEHOLDER is not None:

                    ).inc()

            return False
        key_props = canonicalize_merge_key("ThreatActor", {"name": raw_name})
        aliases = data.get("aliases", [])
        # uses_techniques: list of MITRE technique IDs this actor explicitly uses,
        # extracted from the ATT&CK STIX relationships bundle by the MITRE collector.
        uses_techniques = data.get("uses_techniques", [])

            # 2026-10 (R6): MITRE group → software claims → USES_MALWARE / USES_TOOL (build_relationships 2b/2c)
            "uses_malware": data.get("uses_malware", []) or [],
            "uses_tools": data.get("uses_tools", []) or [],
        }
        if data.get("pulse_id"):
            extra_props["pulse_ids"] = [str(data["pulse_id"])] + [str(x) for x in (data.get("report_ids") or []) if x]
        if data.get("sophistication"):
            extra_props["sophistication"] = data["sophistication"]
        if data.get("primary_motivation"):
            extra_props["primary_motivation"] = data["primary_motivation"]
        if data.get("resource_level"):
            extra_props["resource_level"] = data["resource_level"]
        # 2026-10-16: as in merge_malware — the source ranking decides the description.
        _mark_deprecated(data, extra_props)
        return self.merge_node_with_source(
            "ThreatActor",
            key_props,
            data,
            source_id,
            extra_props=extra_props,
            description=ENTITY_DESCRIPTIONS.record(data.get("description"), source_id),
        )

    def _normalize_mitre_id(self, raw: Any, *, label: str, data: Dict) -> Optional[str]:
        """PR-N16 Fix #2 (BLOCK, 2026-04-22): normalize a MITRE ATT&CK
        id (T####, TA####, S####, G####) to canonical UPPERCASE +
        None-guard.

        Pre-PR-N16, ``merge_technique`` / ``merge_tactic`` /
        ``merge_tool`` stored mitre_ids as-received. ``compute_node_uuid``
        goes through ``canonical_node_key`` which ``.lower()`` the
        joined canonical string — so ``"T1056"`` and ``"t1056"`` compute
        the SAME uuid. But the Cypher ``MERGE (n:Technique {mitre_id:
        $mitre_id})`` is case-sensitive, so two distinct nodes get
        created sharing one uuid. Cross-environment delta-sync hits
        either node non-deterministically → split subgraphs.

        Same asymmetry class as PR #37 (Indicator value canonicalization
        — fixed then) but in MITRE helpers missed at that time.

        MITRE ID convention: uppercase throughout
        (https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1056/). Normalize at
        ingest to uppercase so both MERGE key AND uuid match. Strip
        surrounding whitespace.
        """
        mitre_id = nonempty_graph_string(raw)
        if mitre_id is None:
            logger.warning(
                "[MERGE-REJECT] %s MERGE refused: mitre_id=%r (None / empty / whitespace-only). name=%r",
                label,
                raw,
                data.get("name"),
            )
            return None
        # PR-N16 Fix #2: canonicalize to uppercase — matches both the
        # MITRE spec AND the canonical_node_key's .lower() so the
        # Cypher MERGE key and the uuid don't diverge.
        return mitre_id.upper()

    def merge_technique(self, data: Dict, source_id: str = "mitre_attck") -> bool:
        """MERGE a Technique node with source tracking.

        PR-N13 (2026-04-21 pre-baseline audit Fix #2): reject None /
        empty / whitespace-only ``mitre_id``. Without this, a single
        malformed MITRE tag like ``{"name": "Foo"}`` (no mitre_id)
        hijacks the sentinel ``(Technique {mitre_id: null})`` node
        that every subsequent None-keyed row also collapses into.
        Mirrors the PR-N10 placeholder-name guard for Malware / Actor.

        PR-N16 Fix #2 (2026-04-22 BLOCK): canonicalize mitre_id to
        uppercase via ``_normalize_mitre_id`` so the case-sensitive
        Cypher MERGE key agrees with the case-insensitive uuid
        computation. Prevents split-node / shared-uuid bugs on
        MISP peers storing lowercase ids.

        ``description`` and ``description_source``: as in ``merge_malware`` (2026-10-16).

        ``is_subtechnique``: whether the normalised id is dotted (2026-10), whatever the record says.
        """
        mitre_id = self._normalize_mitre_id(data.get("mitre_id"), label="Technique", data=data)
        if mitre_id is None:
            return False
        key_props = {"mitre_id": mitre_id}
        extra_props: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "tactic_phases": data.get("tactic_phases", []),
            # 2026-10: ATT&CK domain so ICS techniques link only to ICS tactics.
            "attack_domain": str(data.get("attack_domain") or "enterprise"),
        }
        extra_props["detection"] = data.get("detection", "")
        # 2026-10: from the ATT&CK id, as build_relationships step 1b reads it: ATT&CK identifies a
        # sub-technique by its parent's id and a dotted suffix (T1059.001 under T1059). The MISP round
        # trip carries no flag, so reading it from the record wrote the default False onto every
        # sub-technique on each sync.
        extra_props["is_subtechnique"] = "." in mitre_id
        if data.get("name"):
            extra_props["name"] = data["name"]
        # 2026-10-16: the source ranking decides the description (any record used to set it).
        _mark_deprecated(data, extra_props)
        return self.merge_node_with_source(
            "Technique",
            key_props,
            data,
            source_id,
            extra_props=extra_props,
            description=ENTITY_DESCRIPTIONS.record(data.get("description"), source_id),
        )
